records.title: 2-Coloring Cycles in One Round
records.abstract: Formalizes certified upper and lower bounds for one-round randomized algorithms that 2-color cycles.

informal.Distributed2Coloring.pStar_ge_23879: Proves that every one-round classical algorithm has monochromatic-edge probability at least 0.23879.
informal.Distributed2Coloring.pStar_lt_24118: Proves that an explicit one-round algorithm attains monochromatic-edge probability strictly below 0.24118.

records.title: A formalization of Borel determinacy in Lean
records.abstract: Formalizes Martin's theorem that every Borel Gale-Stewart game is determined.

informal.GaleStewartGame.borel_determinacy: Proves that every Borel Gale-Stewart game on a nonempty discrete alphabet is determined.
informal.GaleStewartGame.Games.borel_determinacy: Proves Borel determinacy for the bundled game representation used in the formalization.

records.title: Exceptional Set in the abc Conjecture
records.abstract: Formalizes reductions and optimization bounds for a power-saving estimate on exceptional triples in the abc conjecture.

informal.abcConjecture_iff_countTriples: Recasts the abc conjecture as a uniform big-O bound for bounded exceptional triples.
informal.refinedCountTriplesStar_isBigO_B: Bounds the refined exceptional-triple count by the dyadic structured-box supremum.
informal.thm_4_point_3: Derives the Section 4 optimization bound from the determinant, geometry, and Fourier hypotheses.

records.title: Aumann's Agreement Theorem
records.abstract: Formalizes Aumann's agreement theorem for information partitions and a common-prior setting, together with a p-belief variant bounding posterior disagreement by 2 * (1 - p).

informal.AgreeToDisagree.agreeToDisagree: If it is common knowledge at a state that two agents assign fixed posterior probabilities to an event, and the common-knowledge cell has equal posterior under their priors, then the two posterior probabilities are equal.
informal.AgreeToDisagree.agreeToDisagree': Generalizes the agreement theorem to a family of agents indexed by an arbitrary type.
informal.AgreeToDisagree.agreeToDisagree_beliefs: Proves that common p-belief of fixed posteriors bounds the difference between any two agents' real-valued posteriors by 2 * (1 - p).

records.title: Disproof of the Aharoni-Korman Conjecture
records.abstract: Formalizes Hollom's counterexample to the Aharoni-Korman fishbone conjecture for partially ordered sets.

informal.LeanPool.AharoniKorman.aharoni_korman_fa: Proves that not every partially ordered set has either an infinite antichain or a chain meeting every antichain in a partition.

records.title: The Anderson Conjecture: A Weakly Quasi-Complete Ring Need Not Be Quasi-Complete
records.abstract: Formalizes a counterexample to Anderson's question, constructing a weakly quasi-complete Noetherian local ring that is not quasi-complete via the Jensen-Heitmann-Loepp transfinite construction.

informal.anderson_main_theorem: Proves that there exists a weakly quasi-complete Noetherian local ring that is not quasi-complete.

records.title: Apportionmentlib
records.abstract: Formalizes apportionment rules and proves the Balinski-Young impossibility theorem: no anonymous quota rule can be population-monotone.

informal.Apportionment.balinski_young: Proves that no anonymous quota apportionment rule can satisfy population monotonicity.

records.title: Archon-FirstProof-Results
records.abstract: Collects formal solutions from the Archon FirstProof benchmark, including polynomial and graph-theoretic results.

informal.Problem4.harmonic_mean_inequality_full: Proves the benchmark harmonic-mean inequality for real-rooted polynomial transforms.
informal.Problem6.exists_eps_light_subset: Proves the benchmark light-subset existence theorem in the graph Laplacian setting.

records.title: Artin-Wedderburn Theorem
records.abstract: Formalizes the Artin-Wedderburn theorem for prime and simple Artinian rings.

informal.LeanPool.ArtinWedderburn.ArtinWedderburn: A nontrivial prime Artinian ring is isomorphic to a matrix ring over a division ring.

records.title: The Bannai-Bannai-Stanton Bound on Distance Sets
records.abstract: Formalizes the Bannai-Bannai-Stanton theorem: a distance set `S` in `ℝ^d` realizing `s` distinct distances has size at most `Nat.choose (d + s) s`. Follows the short polynomial-method proof of Petrov and Pohoata via a generalized Croot-Lev-Pach rank lemma, with auxiliary results on the diagonal linear-independence argument for polynomials, monomial counting of bounded degree, and a rank bound for sums of matrices.

informal.BannaiBannaiStanton.bannai_bannai_stanto: A distance set `S` in Euclidean space `ℝ^d` realizing `s` distinct distances satisfies `S.encard ≤ Nat.choose (d + s) s`.

records.title: Chebyshev Quotients and Demazure Multiplicities
records.abstract: Formalizes positivity results for the coefficients of Chebyshev-type polynomial quotients attached to integer partitions, modelling Demazure multiplicities. Proves that the relevant generating function is a polynomial and that its coefficients are eventually positive (Theorem 1), gives explicit Cauchy-product and matrix-inverse formulas for the coefficients (Theorem 2), and establishes their nonnegativity through a Dyck-path lattice counting model (Theorem 3).

informal.Biswal.Theorem1.genFun_is_polynomial: Proves that the generating function attached to a partition is a polynomial whenever its parts are bounded by the parameter `m`.
informal.Biswal.Theorem1.genFun_coeff_eventually_: Proves that the coefficients of the generating function attached to a partition are eventually strictly positive.
informal.Biswal.Theorem23.thm_manifest_coeff_nonn: Proves that every coefficient of the generating function is nonnegative, via the explicit Dyck-path lattice counting model.

records.title: Boolean Isoperimetry and Conway--Guy Coherent Gaps
records.abstract: Formalizes Harper's vertex-isoperimetric theorem for the Boolean cube: among all families of a fixed cardinality, the simplicial initial segment has the smallest closed radius-one Hamming neighborhood. Develops the supporting binomial-cascade identities, Kruskal--Katona shadow bounds, coordinate compressions, and the final dimension induction. Applies the coherent-gap certificate method to prove normalized consecutive-gap rigidity for the Conway--Guy sequence from its exact recurrence.

informal.BooleanIsoperimetry.harper_theorem: For every family of vertices in an n-dimensional Boolean cube, the simplicial initial segment of the same cardinality has a closed radius-one Hamming neighborhood no larger than that of the family.
informal.BooleanIsoperimetry.conwayGuyGapRigidity: In every dimension, any real row whose consecutive subset-sum gaps relative to the Conway--Guy reference row are at least one dominates that row coordinatewise.

records.title: Brauer Group Core
records.abstract: Formalizes central simple algebra infrastructure, Wedderburn-Artin structure theorems, and finite-field triviality for Brauer groups.

informal.BrauerGroup.BruaerGroup: Constructs the Brauer group of a field from Brauer equivalence classes of central simple algebras.
informal.BrauerGroupHom.Br: Constructs the Brauer group functor from fields to commutative groups via scalar extension.
informal.WedderburnArtin: Proves a Wedderburn-Artin decomposition for simple Artinian rings as matrix algebras over division rings.
informal.trivialBrauer: Proves that every element of the Brauer group of a finite field is trivial.
informal.WedderburnArtin_algebra_version: Gives an algebra equivalence form of Wedderburn-Artin for finite-dimensional central simple algebras.
informal.IsCentralSimple.TensorProduct.simple: Proves simplicity of tensor products of central simple algebras over a field.
informal.IsCentralSimple.TensorProduct.isCentral: Proves centrality of tensor products of central algebras over a field.
informal.CSA_implies_CSA: Shows that the division algebra factor in a matrix presentation of a central simple algebra is central over the base field.

records.title: Existence of Nash equilibria via Brouwer's fixed-point theorem
records.abstract: Formalizes Scarf's combinatorial lemma, derives Brouwer's fixed-point theorem on a simplex and on finite products of simplices, and uses it to prove the existence of a mixed Nash equilibrium in every finite game.

informal.ExistsNashEq: Every finite game has a mixed Nash equilibrium.
informal.Brouwer: Every continuous self-map of a standard simplex has a fixed point.
informal.Brouwer_Product: Every continuous self-map of a finite product of simplices has a fixed point.
informal.IndexedLOrder.Scarf: Scarf's combinatorial lemma producing a colorful simplex.
informal.FinGame: The structure of a finite game with finitely many players and finite pure strategy sets.
informal.FinGame.mixedNashEquilibrium: The predicate that a mixed strategy profile is a Nash equilibrium.

records.title: Formalisation of the Bruhat-Tits Tree
records.abstract: Formalizes the Bruhat-Tits tree for GL₂ over the fraction field of a discrete valuation ring.

informal.BruhatTits.BTtree: Proves that the Bruhat-Tits graph is a tree.
informal.BruhatTits.btgraph_regular: Proves regularity of the Bruhat-Tits graph when the residue field is finite.
informal.BruhatTits.BTlaplace_surjective: Proves surjectivity of the Bruhat-Tits Laplacian on harmonic cochains.

records.title: Burkholder Martingale Transform Inequality
records.abstract: Formalizes Burkholder's sharp Lp inequality for real-valued martingale transforms: if `f` is a discrete martingale and `w` a predictable multiplier bounded by `1`, then the Lp norm of the transform `w ⋆ₘ f` is at most `(pStar p - 1)` times the Lp norm of `f`, where `pStar p` is the maximum of `p` and its conjugate exponent. The proof builds the Burkholder special function as a majorant of the relevant payoff in each exponent regime (`1 < p < 2`, `p = 2`, `p > 2`).

informal.MeasureTheory.Lp_Burkholder_inequality_m: The sharp Lp Burkholder inequality: for a discrete martingale `f` and a predictable multiplier `w` with `|w n| ≤ 1`, the Lp norm of the martingale transform `(w ⋆ₘ f) n` is bounded by `(pStar p - 1)` times the Lp norm of `f n`.
informal.MeasureTheory.martingaleTransform_martin: The martingale transform of a martingale by a strongly predictable bounded multiplier is itself a martingale.
informal.Majorants.exists_majorant_p_g_1: For every exponent `p > 1` there exists a Burkholder majorant, the special function dominating the payoff and driving the inequality.

records.title: Finite Čencov-Petz Uniqueness
records.abstract: Formalizes the finite/discrete Čencov-Petz uniqueness theorem, showing that any continuous metric family on finite probability simplexes that is monotone under Markov morphisms is a scalar multiple of the Fisher information metric.

informal.LeanPool.CencovPetz.MonotoneMetricFamily: Proves that every continuous monotone metric family on a finite probability simplex is a scalar multiple of the Fisher information metric.
Establishes the scalar Fisher-form identity at rational simplex points using split representations.
Proves the scalar Fisher-form identity for simplex points represented as pushforwards of uniform distributions under splitting maps.
Shows that the uniform-point scalar is independent of simplex dimension once the dimension is at least two.
informal.LeanPool.CencovPetz.TangentFin.Bilin.B_e: Proves that the permutation-invariant bilinear form at a uniform finite simplex point is a scalar multiple of the Fisher bilinear form.

records.title: Uniqueness of Shannon Capacity-Achieving Priors
records.abstract: Formalizes uniqueness of the capacity-achieving input distribution for a Markov-kernel channel in three aligned layers: a finite-alphabet theorem (compactness, continuity, and strict concavity of mutual information on Mathlib's weak topology for `ProbabilityMeasure`), a concrete discharged theorem for compact-Polish channels with a common strictly positive jointly continuous density, and a general measure-theoretic packaging that isolates the abstract well-conditioning hypotheses, plus a counterexample showing pairwise-distinct rows do not give an injective prior pushforward (the non-degeneracy required for uniqueness).

informal.ChannelCapacity.exists_unique_capacity_a: For a Markov kernel between finite alphabets (nonempty input) whose rows are linearly independent (`Kernel.RowMatrixFullRank`), a capacity-achieving input prior exists and is unique.

For compact-Polish channels with a common strictly positive jointly continuous density, given injectivity of the prior-pushforward map and upper semicontinuity of mutual information (the latter carried as a field of `Kernel.ContinuousPositiveDensity`, not derived), the capacity-achieving prior is unique.
General measure-theoretic packaging: under abstract well-conditioning hypotheses, the capacity-achieving prior is unique.

records.title: A Detailed Proof of the Chudnovsky Formula
records.abstract: Formalizes the Chudnovsky brothers' rapidly convergent series for 1/π, proving Mathlib's `chudnovskySum = π⁻¹`. Follows Milla's elementary complex-analytic proof: Weierstrass and Eisenstein theory, Liouville and parallelogram-residue calculus, the Kummer hypergeometric bridge and the main modular identity relating the j-invariant to the lattice periods, Baker's division-value machinery, and the singular-moduli inputs at the CM point τ = (1 + √-163)/2 — integrality of j(τ) via modular polynomials and Kronecker's congruence, and rationality of the Weierstrass s₂ invariant via Masser's Appendix A.1.

informal.Chudnovsky.chudnovskySum_eq_pi_inv: Proves the Chudnovsky series identity, i.e. Mathlib's `chudnovskySum = π⁻¹`: the series (12 / 640320^(3/2)) · ∑ₙ (-1)ⁿ (6n)! (545140134 n + 13591409) / ((3n)! (n!)³ 640320^(3n)) sums to 1/π.

records.title: Circuit Complexity in Lean 4
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of classical Boolean circuit complexity, including the Shannon counting lower bound, Schnorr's XOR gate lower bound, a gate-elimination lower bound, CNF/DNF lower bounds for parity, and nondeterministic quantification complexity bounds.

informal.CircuitComplexity.shannon_lower_bound_ci: For N at least 6, there exists a Boolean function on N inputs that cannot be computed by any fan-in-2 AND/OR circuit of size at most 2^N / (5N).
informal.CircuitComplexity.schnorr_lower_bound_ci: Any fan-in-2 AND/OR circuit computing the N-input XOR function (or its complement) has at least 2(N-1) internal gates.
informal.CircuitComplexity.Circuit.gate_eliminati: Any circuit over bounded fan-in k AND/OR computing a function with n' essential inputs has size at least n' / k.
informal.CircuitComplexity.DNF.xorBool_complexity: Any DNF formula computing the N-input XOR function requires at least 2^(N-1) terms.
informal.CircuitComplexity.CNF.xorBool_complexity: Any CNF formula computing the N-input XOR function requires at least 2^(N-1) clauses.
informal.CircuitComplexity.existQuantify_complexi: If a function f has circuit complexity s, then the existential quantification of f over a k-bit block has circuit complexity at most 2^k * (s + 1).

records.title: circuitlib: a circuit verification library for Lean 4
records.abstract: A categorical semantics framework for digital circuits over Belnap's four-valued logic, following Ghica-Kaye-Sprunger. Its main theorems prove that combinational circuits (monotone functions on wire vectors) and sequential circuits (causal monotone stream functions) form symmetric monoidal categories, with a verified full adder as demonstration.

informal.Circuit.SequentialCircuitCategory.instSy: The category of sequential circuits, whose morphisms are causal monotone stream functions as in Ghica-Kaye-Sprunger's denotational semantics, is symmetric monoidal, with all coherence laws (pentagon, triangle, hexagons, symmetry) proven.
informal.Circuit.CombinationalCircuitCategory.ins: The category of combinational circuits, with wire counts as objects and monotone wire-vector functions as morphisms, is symmetric monoidal under juxtaposition of wire bundles.
informal.Circuit.SequentialCircuitCategory.tensor: Causality is preserved by parallel composition, the key lemma making sequential circuits closed under the tensor product.
informal.Circuit.BelnapLevel.instSemilatticeSup: Belnap's four truth values under the information order form a join-semilattice, the wire-value semantics in which every circuit denotes a monotone function.
informal.Circuit.CombinationalCircuit.adder_def: Correctness of a full adder assembled categorically from two half adders, gates, braidings, and whiskerings, computing the Boolean sum and carry bits; a demonstration of the framework.

records.title: Classification of Compact Surfaces
records.abstract: Formalizes the classification of compact connected Hausdorff topological 2-manifolds with boundary as the sphere, an orientable normal-form quotient, or a non-orientable normal-form quotient, using triangulation and finite cyclic polygonal presentations.

informal.LeanEval.Topology.ClassificationOfSurfac: Every compact connected Hausdorff topological 2-manifold with boundary is homeomorphic to the sphere, an orientable normal-form quotient, or a non-orientable normal-form quotient.

records.title: Clawristotle: Vlasov-Maxwell-Landau steady-state classification
records.abstract: Formalizes a steady-state classification result for the Vlasov-Maxwell-Landau system with Coulomb kernel.

informal.VML.Theorem42: States the abstract steady-state classification theorem for the Vlasov-Maxwell-Landau framework.
informal.VML.CoulombConcreteTheorem42: Specializes the steady-state classification theorem to the Coulomb kernel.

records.title: Spectral theorem for compact self-adjoint operators
records.abstract: Formalizes the spectral theorem for compact self-adjoint operators on a Hilbert space: such an operator admits a Hilbert basis of eigenvectors. The development passes from weak compactness of Hilbert closed balls and Rayleigh-quotient extrema to an eigenvector at the operator norm, finiteness of the point spectrum outside any neighbourhood of zero, finite-rank cutoff approximation, and finally the orthogonal decomposition into eigenspaces.

informal.CompactSelfAdjoint.exists_hilbertBasis_h: A compact self-adjoint operator on a Hilbert space admits a Hilbert basis of eigenvectors.
informal.CompactSelfAdjoint.iSup_eigenspace_ortho: The eigenspaces of a compact self-adjoint operator span a dense subspace: the orthogonal complement of the supremum of all eigenspaces is trivial.
informal.CompactSelfAdjoint.exists_hasEigenvector: A compact self-adjoint operator has an eigenvector whose eigenvalue realizes either the supremum or the infimum of its Rayleigh quotient.
informal.CompactSelfAdjoint.exists_unit_norm_eq_o: A compact operator attains its operator norm on the unit sphere of the Hilbert space.
informal.CompactSelfAdjoint.countable_set_hasEige: The set of nonzero eigenvalues of a compact self-adjoint operator is countable.

records.title: Hurwitz's Classification of Euclidean Composition Algebras
records.abstract: Formalizes Hurwitz's classification of nontrivial finite-dimensional real Euclidean composition algebras: every such algebra has dimension 1, 2, 4, or 8 and is real-linearly equivalent to the real numbers, complex numbers, quaternions, or octonions through a map preserving the unit, multiplication, and norm form. The development also constructs the octonions from an explicit Fano multiplication table, proves Degen's eight-square identity, and shows that Cayley--Dickson doubling preserves the composition law for associative inputs.

informal.CompositionAlgebra.hurwitz_classificatio: Every nontrivial finite-dimensional real Euclidean composition algebra is linearly equivalent to the real numbers, complex numbers, quaternions, or octonions through a map preserving the unit, multiplication, and norm form.
informal.CompositionAlgebra.finrank_eq_one_or_two: The real dimension of a nontrivial finite-dimensional Euclidean composition algebra is exactly 1, 2, 4, or 8.
informal.CompositionAlgebra.CD.instCompositionAlg: The Cayley--Dickson double of a nontrivial associative Euclidean composition algebra again satisfies the composition law.
informal.Octonion.nucleus_real: Any octonion that associates in the third slot with every pair has zero imaginary coordinates and hence lies on the real line.

records.title: Oracle Computability and Turing Degrees
records.abstract: Formalizes oracle-relative computability via partial recursive functions, Turing reducibility and the Turing degrees as an upper semilattice, a Gödel numbering with a universal oracle machine, the jump operator, and the arithmetical hierarchy.

informal.Computability.RecursiveIn: The inductive relation `RecursiveIn O f` stating that `f : ℕ →. ℕ` is partial recursive relative to a set of oracle functions `O`.
informal.Computability.exists_code_rel: Universality of the oracle evaluator `evalo`, that is, `RecursiveIn (Set.range g) f` holds iff there is a code `c` with `evalo g c = f`.
informal.Computability.TuringReducible: `f` is Turing reducible to `g` (`f ≤ᵀ g`) when `f` is recursive in the singleton oracle set `{g}`.
informal.Computability.TuringDegree: The type of Turing degrees, the antisymmetrization of partial functions under Turing reducibility.
informal.Computability.jump_recIn: The original function is Turing reducible to its jump, `f ≤ᵀ f⌜`.
informal.Computability.TuringDegree.instSemilatti: The Turing degrees form an upper semilattice with the Turing join as supremum.

records.title: Verified interval-Cauchy real arithmetic
records.abstract: Represents real numbers as Cauchy sequences of nested rational intervals quotiented into a field, with executable interval ring arithmetic, proven-convergent rational bounds for sqrt, exp, and pi, and an IsComputable typeclass that packages such approximations to drive classical (noncomputable) comparison instances, after O'Connor's certified exact real computation.

informal.ComputableℝSeq: A sequence of converging rational lower and upper bounds representing a single real number.
informal.Computableℝ: The quotient of interval-Cauchy sequences by equality of value, an ordered field whose ring operations are executable interval arithmetic.
informal.IsComputable: A typeclass packaging an explicit interval-Cauchy approximation of a real number, used to drive its classical comparison instances.
informal.Computableℝ.instField: The field instance on the quotient; inversion extracts a sign witness classically and is noncomputable.
informal.ComputableℝSeq.Sqrt.sqrtq: Computes converging rational interval bounds for the square root of a rational interval.

records.title: Connes-Kreimer Hopf algebra of rooted trees
records.abstract: Formalizes the planar Connes-Kreimer/Foissy Hopf algebra of rooted trees, its cut coproduct, bialgebra and Hopf algebra structures, the commutative quotient, Adams operators, and the Eulerian idempotent on the quotient.

informal.CK.instCKHopf: Constructs the planar rooted-tree Connes-Kreimer/Foissy Hopf algebra as a Mathlib `HopfAlgebra`.
informal.CK.instHabHopf: Constructs the Hopf algebra structure on the commutative quotient of the planar rooted-tree algebra.
informal.CK.eulerian1_idem_ab: Proves that the first Eulerian idempotent is idempotent on the commutative quotient.
informal.CK.coassoc_map: Lifts the list-level cut coassociativity proof to equality of linear maps for the coproduct.
informal.PowerSeries.logOf_mul: Proves additivity of `PowerSeries.logOf` for power series with constant coefficient one.

records.title: Conditional formalization of Zhou's Connes-rigidity counterexample
records.abstract: Constructs Zhou's two countable discrete groups and, assuming the project's universe-polymorphic property-(T) predicate for EL₃(𝔽₂[t]), proves that both satisfy the same predicate, are ICC and nonisomorphic, while their group von Neumann algebras are trace-preservingly normally star-isomorphic.

informal.Connes.theoremA: At any Hilbert-space universe, assuming property-(T) for EL₃(𝔽₂[t]), constructs two countable discrete ICC groups satisfying property-(T) at that universe which are nonisomorphic although their group von Neumann algebras are trace-preservingly normally star-isomorphic.

records.title: The Cramer-Wold theorem
records.abstract: Formalizes the finite-dimensional Cramer-Wold theorem for measures on Euclidean spaces, with Banach-space continuous-dual generalizations, Hilbert-space inner-product versions, and random-variable law corollaries for identical distributions and `HasLaw`.

informal.LeanPool.CramerWold.euclideanSpace_measu: Proves the classical finite-dimensional Cramer-Wold theorem for finite Borel measures on `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)`, showing equality when all scalar projections have equal pushforward measures.
informal.LeanPool.CramerWold.measure_eq_of_forall: Generalizes the extensionality criterion to finite Borel measures on complete second-countable real normed spaces, using all continuous-linear real projections.
Specializes Cramer-Wold extensionality to real Hilbert spaces, using scalar projections of the form `x ↦ ⟪t, x⟫_ℝ`.
informal.LeanPool.CramerWold.identDistrib_of_fora: Proves that two finite-measure random variables are identically distributed when every continuous-linear real projection of them is identically distributed.
Gives the Hilbert-space random-variable version using all scalar inner-product projections.
informal.LeanPool.CramerWold.hasLaw_of_forall_dua: Proves that a random variable has a target law when every continuous-linear real projection has the corresponding projected target law.

records.title: Counting Critical Portraits
records.abstract: Formalizes the census of degree-d critical portraits, modeled as level-canonical (d-1)-subsets of the cyclic group ZMod (d*m), and proves that their number equals C(d*m, d-1)/d for all d, via the Dvoretzky-Motzkin cycle lemma together with an explicit level-canonicalization bijection (injectivity and surjectivity of the delete-minimum map).

informal.CriticalPortraits.card_portraits: The number of degree-d critical portraits at level m equals C(d*m, d-1)/d.
informal.CriticalPortraits.Cycle.cycle_lemma: The Dvoretzky-Motzkin cycle lemma: a period-n integer sequence with period-sum 1 has exactly one good cyclic shift.
informal.CriticalPortraits.T_injOn: The delete-minimum map is injective on critical portraits.
informal.CriticalPortraits.T_surjOn: The delete-minimum map surjects onto the level-canonical subsets.

records.title: Period Lengths of Rational Cut-and-Project Gap Sequences
records.abstract: Formalizes the closed-form minimal periods of one-dimensional rational cut-and-project gap sequences at the level of the paper's residue model, plus a fully geometric aperiodicity theorem for irrational slopes. For coprime α, β ∈ ℕ and window parameter ω ≥ 0, write N = ⌊ωα⌋ + ⌊ωβ⌋ + 1 and D = α² + β². The strip-to-residue reduction of the paper — sorting the hits of the length-N progression twisted by the geometric multiplier −αβ⁻¹ (mod D) — is taken as the definition of the gap sequence rather than derived from the lattice; for it, the multiset convention has minimal period N/D when D ∣ N and N otherwise, and the set convention (multiplicities flattened to {0,1}) has minimal period 1 when N ≥ D and N otherwise. The irrational case is geometric from first principles: for positive irrational slope and ω > 0, the accepted points of ℤ² sorted by the physical projection have a gap sequence with no finite period, via injectivity of the projection and Kronecker density of the internal image.

informal.CutAndProject.main_theorem_geometric_con: The gap sequence of the residue model of the rational cut-and-project multiset (sorted hits of the length-N progression under the multiplier −αβ⁻¹ mod D) has minimal period N/D if D divides N and N otherwise, where N = ⌊ωα⌋ + ⌊ωβ⌋ + 1 and D = α² + β².
informal.CutAndProject.set_main_theorem_geometric: The set-convention residue-model gap sequence (multiplicities flattened to {0,1}) has minimal period 1 if N ≥ D and N otherwise.
informal.CutAndProject.Irrational.prop_irrational: For positive irrational slope and window parameter ω > 0, the projected gap sequence has no finite period.

records.title: Dead Ends in Square-Free Digit Walks
records.abstract: Formalizes the density formula for base-b dead ends in square-free digit walks.

informal.LeanPool.DeadEnds.baseBDeadEnd_density_f: Proves the inclusion-exclusion density formula for base-b dead ends.

records.title: Extended Demazure Product on ASP Permutations
records.abstract: Formalizes the extended Demazure product on almost-sign-preserving integer permutations, including slipface models, residuals, greedy and stingy characterizations, reduction theorems, adjacent-transposition formulas, and 321-avoiding factorization results.

informal.LeanPool.DemazureProduct.AspPerm.star: Defines the extended Demazure product on almost-sign-preserving permutations.
informal.LeanPool.DemazureProduct.AspPerm.star_as: Proves associativity of the extended Demazure product on almost-sign-preserving permutations.
informal.LeanPool.DemazureProduct.Reduction.starG: Characterizes the Demazure product as the Bruhat-maximum of ordinary products of smaller factors.
informal.LeanPool.DemazureProduct.Reduction.reduc: Reduces inequalities against a Demazure product to ordinary products of Bruhat-smaller factors with fixed shift.
informal.LeanPool.DemazureProduct.Reduction.lres_: Gives the stingy characterization of the left residual as a Bruhat-minimum of ordinary products.
informal.LeanPool.DemazureProduct.ReducedProducts: Shows that the Demazure product equals ordinary multiplication exactly for reduced ASP products.
Proves the adjacent-transposition formula for multiplying an ASP permutation by a no-consecutive-pair involution.
informal.LeanPool.DemazureProduct.ASP321a.dprod_e: Characterizes Demazure factorizations of 321-avoiding ASP permutations by isolated inversion-set decompositions.
informal.LeanPool.DemazureProduct.Tableaux.setVal: Relates fixed-shift set-valued tableaux to Hecke factorizations of 321-avoiding ASP permutations.

records.title: Demazure Operators and Lean
records.abstract: Formalizes Demazure operators on multivariate polynomials and their nilpotence, braid, commutation, and symmetric-polynomial linearity relations, with auxiliary Coxeter-theory support including strong exchange and a conditional Matsumoto theorem.

informal.Demazure.Dem: Defines the Demazure operator as a linear map over the subalgebra of symmetric polynomials.
informal.Demazure.demazure_order_two: Proves that applying the Demazure operator twice gives zero.
informal.Demazure.demazure_commutes_adjacent: Proves the braid relation for adjacent Demazure operators.
informal.Demazure.demazure_commutes_non_adjacent: Proves that non-adjacent Demazure operators commute.
informal.Demazure.demazure_mul_symm: Proves that symmetric polynomials act as scalars with respect to Demazure operators.
informal.CoxeterSystem.strongExchangeProperty: Proves the strong exchange property for Coxeter systems.
informal.CoxeterSystem.matsumoto_reduced: Auxiliary theorem proving, under the extra MatsumotoCondition hypothesis, that reduced words for the same Coxeter group element are connected by braid moves.

records.title: Axiomatic projective geometry (Faure–Frölicher)
records.abstract: Develops, following Faure and Frölicher's Modern Projective Geometry, the axiomatic theory of projective geometries given by a ternary collinearity relation, with subspaces and subgeometries, proves that the central projection between two lines is a bijection, and exhibits every Mathlib projectivization as a projective geometry. Groundwork from the upstream desargues repository — Desargues' theorem itself is not formalized.

informal.Basic.ProjectiveGeometry: Axiomatizes a projective geometry as a typeclass (axioms L₁–L₃, Faure–Frölicher p. 26) on a ternary collinearity relation.
informal.Basic.centralProjection: Defines the central projection of a line onto another from a center point.
informal.Basic.cen_proj_bij: The headline theorem — the central projection between two lines is a bijection.

records.title: Directed Topology in Lean 4
records.abstract: Foundational library for directed topological spaces, dipaths, dihomotopy, the fundamental category functor, and a directed Van Kampen pushout theorem.

informal.DirectedSpace: Definition of a directed topological space as a topological space with a class of directed paths closed under constant paths, concatenation, and monotone reparametrization.
informal.Dipath: A directed path in a directed space.
informal.Dipath.Dihomotopic: Dihomotopy equivalence relation on dipaths between fixed endpoints.
informal.DirectedVanKampen.directed_van_kampen: Proves the directed Van Kampen theorem, showing that the directed fundamental category functor sends the standard open cover square to a pushout in the category of categories.

records.title: Euclidean Distance Geometry
records.abstract: Develops the basepoint-centered Gram approach to finite Euclidean distance geometry. Proves both directions of Schoenberg's characterization, including a rank-controlled factorization of positive-semidefinite matrices; proves that three affinely independent centers in Euclidean three-space determine at most two points with prescribed distances; and verifies the Cayley--Menger determinant for segments and triangles, including the triangle-area identity underlying Heron's formula.

informal.DistanceGeometry.schoenberg: For n at least one, a symmetric hollow n-by-n matrix is a squared-distance matrix of points in k-dimensional Euclidean space exactly when its basepoint-centered Gram matrix is positive semidefinite and has rank at most k.
informal.DistanceGeometry.encard_setOf_forall_dis: In a finite-dimensional real inner-product affine space, prescribed distances to centers whose affine span has codimension one admit at most two solutions.
informal.DistanceGeometry.trilateration_le_two: Three affinely independent centers in three-dimensional Euclidean space admit at most two points with any prescribed triple of distances.
informal.DistanceGeometry.cayleyMenger_det_heron: The Cayley--Menger determinant of three planar points equals minus sixteen times the squared area of their triangle.

records.title: DomainTheory
records.abstract: Formalizes Dana Scott's domain theory through Scott information systems and PRG-19 neighbourhood systems, including approximable maps, products, function spaces, fixed points, recursive presentations, and initial-algebra constructions for denotational semantics.

informal.InfoSys: Defines Scott information systems, with a distinguished bottom token, finite consistency predicate, entailment relation, and Scott's six axioms.
informal.Domain.Neighborhood.NeighborhoodSystem: Defines PRG-19 neighbourhood systems, Scott's neighbourhood presentation of domains.
informal.Domain.Neighborhood.ApproximableMap: Defines approximable maps between neighbourhood systems as relations preserving finite approximations.
informal.Domain.Neighborhood.trianglelefteq_of_is: Proves that an initial algebra for a functor embeds into every other solution through Scott's subdomain relation.
informal.ScottMap.fix_eq: Proves the fixed-point equation for Scott-continuous self maps on complete lattices.

records.title: Duality theory in linear optimization and its extensions
records.abstract: Formalizes Farkas-like theorems and strong LP duality, including extensions to a linearly ordered field with bot and top.

informal.equalityFarkas: Farkas' lemma for linear equalities over nonnegative variables.
informal.inequalityFarkas: Farkas' lemma for linear inequalities over nonnegative variables.
informal.extendedFarkas: Extended Farkas theorem for matrices and vectors over a linearly ordered field with bot and top.
informal.ValidELP.strongDuality: Strong duality theorem for extended linear programs.
informal.StandardLP.strongDuality: Strong duality theorem for linear programs in standard form.

records.title: Weierstrass models and singular points for Tate's algorithm
records.abstract: Formalizes Weierstrass models of elliptic curves over a commutative ring, their b- and c-invariants and discriminant, the change-of-coordinates group action, the discriminant's membership in the Jacobian ideal, and the construction of the singular point of a singular model over a perfect field, together with the Kronecker symbol and the Kodaira type enumeration.

informal.Model: Defines a Weierstrass model of a possibly singular elliptic curve by its five a-invariants.
informal.Model.discr_identity: Proves the identity relating the discriminant to the c-invariants, 1728 * discr = c4^3 - c6^2.
informal.Model.rst_discr: Proves that the discriminant is invariant under the rst change-of-coordinates transformation.
informal.Model.discr_in_jacobian_ideal: Expresses the discriminant as an explicit combination of the Weierstrass polynomial and its partial derivatives, witnessing membership in the Jacobian ideal.
informal.Model.discr_eq_zero_of_singular: Proves that a model with a singular point has vanishing discriminant.
informal.Model.Field.isSingularPoint_singularPoin: Proves that the explicitly constructed singular point of a singular model over a perfect field is indeed a singular point (Connell, Proposition 1.5.4).
informal.Model.Field.move_singular_point_to_origi: Proves that the change of coordinates moving the singular point places it at the origin.
informal.Kodaira: Enumerates the Kodaira reduction types, including the extra types arising over imperfect residue fields of characteristic 2 or 3.

records.title: The Erdős–Graham–Ruzsa–Straus two-prime theorem
records.abstract: A complete machine-checked proof that for any two distinct odd primes p and q there are infinitely many n with binom(2n,n) coprime to pq, including the iterated carry-controlled digit-clearing step that Bloom and Croot defer to the 1975 paper, via a per-move lexicographic measure, an elementary staircase lemma, and a Dirichlet-approximation seed.

informal.Egrs75.MuFinish.egrs_two_prime_mu: Proves that for distinct odd primes p and q there are infinitely many n with p and q both not dividing the central binomial coefficient binom(2n,n), via the mu-measure descent.
informal.Egrs75.Finish.egrs_two_prime_finish: Reassembles the same theorem via bad-bit-mask strong induction, with the low-case clearing discharged by Egrs75.MuFinish.egrs_clearing_low_mu.
informal.Egrs75.not_dvd_centralBinom_iff_lowDigit: The Kummer bridge, stating that an odd prime p does not divide binom(2n,n) exactly when every base-p digit of n is at most (p-1)/2.
informal.Egrs75.MathlibAPI.irrational_log_div_log: Proves that the ratio of logarithms of two distinct primes is irrational.

records.title: The Convex-Octagon Case of Erdős Problem 97
records.abstract: Proves that among eight labelled points in the Euclidean plane in convex position, at least one point has no four other points at a common distance. The development reduces a geometric counterexample to a finite incidence model, classifies normalized row patterns up to symmetry, proves geometric and algebraic obstructions, and excludes seven canonical first-row masks with a kernel-audited exhaustive search over the remaining legal row masks and checked geometric obstruction witnesses. This is the modern four-equidistant formulation; Erdős's 1946 paper posed the stronger three-equidistant version. This is the convex-octagon case only; the general Erdős Problem 97 remains open.

informal.Erdos97Octagon.erdos97_convex_octagon: Among eight labelled points in the Euclidean plane in convex position, some point has no four other points at a common distance.

records.title: Leo Moser's finite distinct-subset-sums inequality
records.abstract: Formalizes the exact finite sum-of-squares inequality that Guy's 1982 account states as Theorem 2 and attributes to Leo Moser: a finite set A of natural numbers with distinct subset sums satisfies 4^|A| - 1 <= 3 * sum(a^2). It then derives direct and square-root lower bounds for the largest element of A. This does not claim the stronger historical asymptotic bound attributed jointly to Erdős and Moser, and Erdős Problem 1 remains open.

informal.LeanPool.ErdosMoser.leoMoserVarianceBoun: If a finite set A of natural numbers has distinct subset sums, then 4^|A| - 1 is at most three times the sum of the squares of the elements of A.
informal.LeanPool.ErdosMoser.erdosMoserMaxBound: For a nonempty finite set A of natural numbers with distinct subset sums, 4^|A| - 1 is at most 3|A| times the square of its largest element.
informal.LeanPool.ErdosMoser.erdosMoserMaxSqrt: The equivalent square-root lower bound on the largest element: sqrt((4^|A| - 1)/(3|A|)) is at most max(A).

records.title: The Erdős–Tuza–Valtr conjecture
records.abstract: Formalizes the Erdős–Tuza–Valtr conjecture, a sharp refinement of the Erdős–Szekeres happy-ending theorem, proving that any general-position point set of size at least C(n+2,2)+2 contains the target cup–cap configuration.

informal.ErdosTuzaValtr.main: Proves the sharp upper bound — a general-position point set with at least C(n+2,2)+2 points contains the Erdős–Tuza–Valtr cup–cap configuration.
informal.Config.main_lemma: The configuration-relative induction lemma that, with the mirror-symmetry reduction, drives the main proof.

records.title: Primitive Sets Above x (Erdos Problem 1196)
records.abstract: Formalizes Math Inc.'s proof around primitive sets above x for Erdos Problem 1196.

informal.Erdos1196.erdos_1196: States the formalized version of Erdos Problem 1196.

records.title: Convex Three-Distance Degree-Six Theorem and Exceptional-Word Closures
records.abstract: Proves that every finite cyclically strictly convex planar configuration has a vertex incident to at most six edges from its three largest distance classes. The proof selects a maximal-gap vertex and coordinated majorants, closes all exceptional inner branches, performs the five-row enumeration, and transports all thirteen canonical cover words to four shared full-two-rung, anti-saturation, terminal-cage, and four-edge-cage predicates. It also proves exceptional-count rigidity and an explicit heptagon refutation of a tempting stronger majorant claim, with rational regression witnesses. This settles the all-n k=3 instance of the paper's suggested degree-2k convex bound; Morić--Pritchard proved the corresponding top-three edge bound for sufficiently large n. It does not settle the general-k suggestion or the general Erdős problem 132.

informal.LeanPool.Erdos132ConvexK3.convex_top_thr: For every nonempty finite cyclically strictly convex planar configuration with three strictly ordered largest squared-distance classes d₁, d₂, and d₃, some vertex is incident to at most six pairs whose squared distance is one of those three classes.

Cyclic strict convexity and the three-largest-distance-class hypothesis construct the full maximal-gap, thirteen-word reduction package together with route-specific closure evidence, without any remaining coordinated-majorant or geometric-adapter assumption.
informal.LeanPool.Erdos132ConvexK3.global_thirtee: Every one of the thirteen canonical maximal-gap cover words transports to its routed full-two-rung, anti-saturation, terminal-cage, or four-edge-cage realization, and hence supplies the corresponding degree bound.
informal.LeanPool.Erdos132ConvexK3.concrete_word_: A thirteen-tag routing interface over four shared geometric realization predicates maps B:3→2 and D:3→2 to Row1B32WordRealization, B:3→1, BA, D:3→1, and DC to OnePenultimateWordGeometry, DD to Row4DDWordRealization, and the remaining six tags to FullTwoRungGeometry. Each inhabited routed predicate supplies a vertex of degree at most six, with the one-penultimate route proving the stronger bound five.
informal.LeanPool.Erdos132ConvexK3.fullTwoRung_re: Every raw full-two-rung realization has its displayed vertex of degree at most six. A rigid normalization derives the canonical coordinates, the diameter branch is impossible, the long branch is counted from four raw boundary arcs, and the short branch contradicts the exact two-rung identity and metric dichotomy.
informal.LeanPool.Erdos132ConvexK3.convex_k3_degr: This implication from the abstract reduction interface is retained as the final assembly map. Its hypothesis is now discharged by convex_top_three_draft_reduction_complete, yielding the unconditional theorem convex_top_three_degree_six; ErLV89 itself proves only the degree-eight bound obtained from 3k−1 when k=3.
informal.LeanPool.Erdos132ConvexK3.coordinated_ex: Every exceptional jointly minimal pair lies in case (1,2), (2,1), or (2,2). In (1,2), every first substitute has at least one right move while every second substitute has exactly two left moves and zero right moves. In (2,1), every first substitute has exactly two right moves and zero left moves while every second substitute has at least one left move. Only in (2,2) are those exact substitute counts proved on both sides.

Assuming the three top distance classes and TopThreeAdjacent for both starting edges z–x and t–u, each forced two-move chain in an exceptional inner-move case has the rank ladder from the third-largest through the second-largest to the largest distance, while its proposed intermediate exchange edge remains nonterminal.
informal.LeanPool.Erdos132ConvexK3.heptagon_nondi: In an explicit rational convex heptagon, a second-largest-distance edge is already terminal under both permitted cover moves, refuting the stronger claim that every non-diameter top-three edge admits a longer cover.
informal.LeanPool.Erdos132ConvexK3.Witnesses.nine: An explicit rational nine-point regression configuration realizes squared-distance classes 855625, 838525, and 811165 as its three largest classes.
informal.LeanPool.Erdos132ConvexK3.Witnesses.rati: An explicit rational six-point regression configuration realizes the three stated rational squared-distance values as its largest classes.

records.title: A Conditional Fourteen-Point Case of Erdős Problem 132
records.abstract: Formalizes the planar Hopf--Pannwitz diameter bound and proves the fourteen-point low-multiplicity conclusion conditional on exactly two remaining published interfaces: the known maximum-cardinality bound for planar sets with at most six distances and the Szöllősi--Östergård classification of thirteen-point planar six-distance sets. Internally derives the exact failure profile and endpoint deletion, constructs the three classified templates, eliminates the nonregular cases by multiplicity, and excludes the regular tridecagon extension by explicit second and fourth moments. The general Erdős problem remains open.

informal.LeanPool.Erdos132N14.hopfPannwitzLowMult: Every injectively labelled fourteen-point planar configuration has a realized distance represented by at most fourteen unordered pairs; the proof chooses that distance to be a diameter.
informal.LeanPool.Erdos132N14.erdos132_for_fourte: Assuming precisely the published planar few-distance cardinality and Szöllősi--Östergård classification interfaces, every injectively labelled fourteen-point planar configuration realizes at least two distances whose unordered-pair multiplicities are at most fourteen.

records.title: Planar Point Sets Whose Non-Diameter Distances Form a Geometric 3-Chain
records.abstract:
Formalizes a support theorem about planar point sets whose non-diameter squared distances are confined to a geometric progression of ratio three. The chain-quadruple theorem shows that no planar quadruple with all six squared distances in such a chain can span two chain steps, and classifies the seven labelled patterns that do occur: the rhombus of two glued equilateral triangles, in five positions of its long edge, and the equilateral triangle with its centroid, in two. A Gram obstruction then rules out any five-point chain configuration. The lift to n at least thirteen runs through the diameter graph: the Caro--Wei independence bound, proved here, produces an independent five-set once the diameter graph is known to have at most as many edges as the set has points. That edge bound is the Hopf--Pannwitz theorem of 1934, and it already exists in the pool; this project reproves it in its own model as a supporting lemma, claiming no novelty for it, and the overlap is set out in full below. The result is unconditional.
There is no prior write-up behind this development. The restriction to ratio 3 is ad hoc: the 3-chain statement was produced by the author's automated research pipeline in August 2026, while the cited source poses the ambient Erdos problem and does not state this restriction or result. This theorem does not resolve Erdos 132, whose distance spectra need not be geometric 3-chains. The descriptive labels used in the Lean docstrings are internal to this development and refer to no numbered result elsewhere.
Overlap disclosure. Erdos132ThreeChain.hopfPannwitz is NOT offered as a new result. The pooled project Erdos132N14 already contains the same diameter bound, and the version here exists only so that this project is self-contained. Its statement, verbatim from LeanPool/Erdos132N14/HopfPannwitz.lean, is

    theorem diameterEdges_card_le
        (P : Configuration ι) (S : Finset ι) {d : ℝ}
        (hd : 0 < d)
        (hmax : ∀ f ∈ pairs S, P.pairDistance f ≤ d) :
        (diameterEdges P S d).card ≤ S.card

where, from LeanPool/Erdos132N14/Basic.lean, `Configuration ι` is a structure carrying an injective `point : ι → ℂ`, `pairs S = (S ×ˢ S).filter fun e ↦ e.1 < e.2` for a `LinearOrder ι`, `pairDistance P e = dist (P.point e.1) (P.point e.2)`, and `diameterEdges P S d = (pairs S).filter fun e ↦ P.pairDistance e = d`. The corresponding statement here is

    theorem hopfPannwitz {X : Finset Point} {D : ℝ} (hD : IsSqDiameter X D) :
        ∑ v ∈ X, degree (DiameterAdj D) X v ≤ 2 * X.card

with `Point = ℝ × ℝ`, `sqDist` the squared Euclidean distance, `DiameterAdj D p q = (p ≠ q ∧ sqDist p q = D)`, `degree adj X v = (X.filter (adj v)).card`, and `IsSqDiameter X D` asserting that `D` is realised by two distinct points of `X` and dominates every squared distance inside `X`. The two are the same mathematical theorem — a positive maximal distance is realised at most as often as there are points — carried by different models: an injective map from a linearly ordered index type into the complex plane, counting a Finset of unordered pairs, against a Finset of points of the real plane, in squared distances and degree-sum form. Neither statement is an instance of the other without a model bridge: a LinearOrder on ℝ × ℝ, a dist-to-sqDist transfer, and a handshake lemma. The proofs differ too, Perles charging there against pendant deletion driven by Cramer's rule here. No project in the pool imports another, and CONTRIBUTING.md records that independence as the property the fast per-project build relies on, so this project reproves the bound rather than importing it. It is a supporting lemma of this development, not one of its results, and it is therefore not listed among the main results below.
Two supporting identities also exist elsewhere in the pool. From LeanPool/Erdos97ConvexOctagon/CayleyMenger.lean,

    theorem cm4_sqDist_eq_zero (a b c d : Plane) :
        cm4 (sqDist a b) (sqDist a c) (sqDist a d)
          (sqDist b c) (sqDist b d) (sqDist c d) = 0

over `Plane = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)` is the same four-point Cayley--Menger vanishing as this project's

    theorem gramDet_eq_zero (a b c d : Point) :
        gramDet (sqDist a b) (sqDist a c) (sqDist a d) (sqDist b c) (sqDist b d) (sqDist c d) = 0

over `Point = ℝ × ℝ`; both are one-line `ring` identities in the coordinates. From LeanPool/DistanceGeometry/SchoenbergHard.lean,

    theorem schoenberg {D : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ} (hD : IsPreDistMatrix D) :
        EmbedsIn D k ↔ (centeredGram D).PosSemidef ∧ (centeredGram D).rank ≤ k

characterizes Euclidean distance matrices in general dimension. This project never invokes it: the four-point condition is used directly as a `ring` identity and the five-point obstruction is a sum-of-squares contradiction, so no positive-semidefiniteness criterion is needed.

informal.Erdos132ThreeChain.nonDiameterSqDists_ne: Let n be at least thirteen, let a be positive, and let X be a finite set of points of the real plane with exactly n elements. Suppose D is the squared diameter of X, meaning that D is realised by two distinct points of X and dominates every squared distance inside X. Then for every natural number h, the set of squared distances realised by distinct points of X and different from D is not equal to the geometric 3-chain consisting of a times 3^j for j below h.
informal.Erdos132ThreeChain.four_chain_adjacent: Let a be positive and let S be a four-element set of points of the real plane such that every squared distance between distinct points of S equals a times a nonnegative power of three. Then there is a positive r, itself equal to a times a nonnegative power of three, for which every squared distance between distinct points of S equals r or 3r.
informal.Erdos132ThreeChain.pair_classification: Let c be positive and let A, B, C, D be points of the real plane with the squared distance from A to B equal to c and every other pairwise squared distance equal to c times a nonnegative power of three. Then each of the four squared distances from A and B to C and to D equals c or 3c, at least one of the two squared distances from A and B to C equals c, likewise for D, the squared distance from C to D equals c or 3c, the squared distance from A to C equals c or that from B to D equals c, the squared distance from B to C equals c or that from A to D equals c, and the whole labelling is one of exactly seven explicit patterns: five with a single edge of squared length 3c, and two in which the three edges of squared length 3c form a triangle.
informal.Erdos132ThreeChain.no_five_chain_finset: Let a be positive. There is no five-element set of points of the real plane in which every squared distance between distinct points equals a times a nonnegative power of three.
informal.Erdos132ThreeChain.no_four_on_circle: Let c be positive. There are no four points of the real plane, each at squared distance c from a common point, whose six pairwise squared distances all equal c or 3c.
informal.Erdos132ThreeChain.carowei: Let adj be a symmetric irreflexive relation with decidable adjacency on a type, and let V be a finite set of vertices. Then V has a subset S, no two elements of which are adjacent, whose cardinality is at least the sum over v in V of one divided by one plus the number of neighbours of v inside V.
informal.Erdos132ThreeChain.exists_independent_fi: Let adj be a symmetric irreflexive relation with decidable adjacency on a type, and let V be a finite set of at least thirteen vertices whose degrees inside V sum to at most twice the cardinality of V. Then V has a five-element subset no two elements of which are adjacent.
informal.Erdos132ThreeChain.chainTwo_nonDiameter_: There is a five-element set of points of the real plane whose squared diameter is 4 and whose set of non-diameter squared distances is exactly the two-term geometric 3-chain consisting of 1 and 3. The configuration that the headline forbids for at least thirteen points is therefore realisable at five points with chain length two.

records.title: Erdős Problem #137: powerful products of consecutive integers
records.abstract: Formalizes the abc-conditional finiteness results for Erdős Problem #137 (Erdős–Selfridge): a number N is powerful if every prime dividing N has its square dividing N, and the question is whether the product F(k,n) = n(n+1)⋯(n+k-1) of k ≥ 3 consecutive integers can be powerful for infinitely many n. Each route isolates its abc input (a radical lower bound) as a single explicit hypothesis and proves everything else outright, concluding that, conditionally, F(k,n) is powerful for only finitely many n for each fixed k ≥ 3.

informal.Erdos137.erdos137_finite: Under the Granville–Langevin radical bound RadLB k (an abc-conditional hypothesis) and k ≥ 3, the set of n ≥ 1 for which F(k,n) is powerful is finite.
informal.Erdos137.erdos137_eventually_not_powerfu: Under RadLB k and k ≥ 3, there is a threshold beyond which F(k,n) is never powerful.
informal.Erdos137.lemma_star: Unconditionally, the radical squared times the powerful part of m is at most m squared (rad m ^ 2 * B2 m ≤ m ^ 2).
informal.Erdos137.powerful_rad_sq_le: A nonzero powerful number N satisfies rad N ^ 2 ≤ N.

records.title: Erdős Problem 346: Ratio Limit Forces the Golden Ratio
records.abstract: Formalizes the limit-exists interpretation of Erdős Problem 346: for a strictly increasing positive integer sequence with a uniform ratio gap whose finite deletions are complete but whose infinite deletions are not, if the consecutive quotient sequence converges to some real limit greater than one, then that limit must equal the golden ratio and the quotient sequence tends to it.

informal.Erdos346.intended_problem_if_limit_exist: Existence of any limit greater than one for the quotient sequence forces convergence to the golden ratio, the intended Erdős–Graham conclusion.
informal.Erdos346.ratio_limit_eq_goldenRatio: If the quotient sequence converges to a limit greater than one under the completeness and incompleteness deletion hypotheses, that limit equals the golden ratio.
informal.Erdos346.ratio_tendsto_goldenRatio_of_li: Under the same hypotheses, the quotient sequence converges to the golden ratio itself.

records.title: Erdős Problem #367
records.abstract: Formalizes upper and lower bound results for powerful parts of products of consecutive integers, including abc-conditional upper bounds, an unconditional odd r-full lower bound, a Pell-style limsup theorem, and polynomial arithmetic cores.

informal.Erdos367.erdos_367_k3: Proves an abc-conditional k = 3 upper bound for the product of square-full parts of three consecutive integers.
informal.GeneralK.B2_upper_bound: Proves a general-k upper bound for the square-full part of a product of consecutive integers from an explicit radical lower-bound hypothesis.
informal.RFullOdd.erdos367_iv: Gives an unconditional odd r construction where the product of r-full parts of two consecutive integers is larger than the stated power of n.
informal.Erdos367.erdos367: Proves an unconditional limsup form showing that the product of square-full parts of three consecutive integers exceeds any fixed multiple of n squared times log n.
informal.Core139.T3: Proves the integer-form arithmetic core yielding the E3 at least 13/9 lower-bound construction under explicit prime-supply data.
informal.Core4027.IDENT: Verifies the degree-27 polynomial identity used in the Davenport-Zannier construction.
informal.Core4027.T3: Proves the integer-form arithmetic core yielding the E3 at least 40/27 lower-bound construction under explicit prime-supply data.

records.title: Sums of Distinct Factorials That Are Powers of Two (Erdos Problem 403)
records.abstract: Reconstructs the finiteness theorem for Erdos Problem 403: only finitely many sums of distinct factorials are powers of two, and every such power is at most 2^7 = 128 (the extremal solution 2! + 3! + 5! = 128). The sharp bound is proved in the factorial number system via a single fixed modulus 12!, with all computations kernel-pure.

informal.Erdos403.erdos_403_sharp: Every power of two that is a sum of distinct factorials is at most 2^7, with 128 the largest solution.
informal.Erdos403.erdos_403_finite: Only finitely many sums of distinct factorials are powers of two.

records.title: Finitely generated cones and finite LP duality
records.abstract: Proves that finitely generated cones in real normed spaces are closed, including a conic Carathéodory reduction and PointedCone API forms. Derives a finite-dimensional inequality form of Farkas' lemma and proves packing attainment with equality to the covering infimum for finite covering and packing linear programs. The Farkas and LP statements overlap the pooled Duality development; the generic cone-closedness results provide the project's distinct reusable API.

informal.LeanPool.Erdos81PaperIContrib.fg_cone_is: The cone generated by a finite family in a real normed vector space is a closed set.
informal.LeanPool.Erdos81PaperIContrib.farkas_ge: An infeasible finite system of nonnegative linear inequalities admits a nonnegative separating Farkas certificate.
informal.LeanPool.Erdos81PaperIContrib.covering_p: Given a finite nonnegative matrix with a strictly positive entry in every column and nonnegative capacities, there is a feasible nonnegative packing whose unit-objective value is maximal and equals the infimum cost of nonnegative coverings with unit demand.

records.title: Near-perfect triangle packings from sum-zero triples
records.abstract: Records a reusable formalization byproduct accompanying Paper III: pairwise edge-disjoint triangles in any finite complete graph such that every vertex is incident to at most three uncovered edges, using a cyclic-group sum-zero triple system, with a bridge to Mathlib's SimpleGraph API.

informal.SumZeroTriangles.exists_simpleGraph_tria: For every finite vertex type, its complete simple graph has a family of pairwise edge-disjoint triangle graphs whose uncovered graph has degree at most three at every vertex.
informal.SumZeroTriangles.exists_triangle_packing: Every finite complete graph has a family of pairwise edge-disjoint triangles leaving uncovered degree at most three at every vertex.

records.title: A sharp 5/8 bound for Erdős Problem 865
records.abstract: Formalizes the resolution of Erdős Problem 865 on pairwise sums. For A ⊆ {1,…,N}, a pairwise-sum triple is a set of distinct a, b, c ∈ A with a+b, a+c, b+c all in A, and A is triple-free when it has none. The development proves that every triple-free A ⊆ [1,N] satisfies 8·|A| ≤ 5·N + 53, that any A exceeding this bound contains a triple, and — via the construction A = [M,2M] ∪ [4M,8M] for N = 8M — that the constant 5/8 is optimal, so f₃(N) = 5N/8 + O(1). The upper bound runs through a folded additive lemma over ℤ/mℤ (a four-set union bound) and a folding lemma, closed by strong induction on N.

informal.Erdos865.erdos865_upper_bound: Every triple-free set A ⊆ [1,N] satisfies 8·|A| ≤ 5·N + 53, i.e. |A| ≤ (5/8)·N + O(1).
informal.Erdos865.erdos865_contains_triple: Every A ⊆ [1,N] with 5·N + 53 < 8·|A| contains a pairwise-sum triple (the paper's Theorem 1.1 form).
informal.Erdos865.sharpness: For N = 8M with M ≥ 1 there is a triple-free A ⊆ [1,N] with 8·|A| = 5·N + 16, so the constant 5/8 is optimal.

records.title: Event Structures and Causal-Consistent Reversibility
records.abstract: Formalizes event structures with binary conflict, their configurations, computations, the trace monoid, and causal-consistent reversibility, proving correctness and causal-safety of rollback, uniqueness of minimal and maximal replays, and conditional replay-existence characterizations.

informal.EventStructures.EventStructure: Defines an event structure as a partially ordered set of events with an irreflexive symmetric conflict relation.
informal.EventStructures.Conf: Defines a configuration as a conflict-free, downward-closed set of events.
informal.EventStructures.Rollback.rollback_correc: Proves that the original configuration is reachable from the rollback of an event when the configuration is finitely representable.
informal.EventStructures.Rollback.rollback_causal: Proves causal safety of rollback - events causally after the rolled-back event are removed.
informal.EventStructures.Replay.minReplay_unique: Proves uniqueness of the minimal replay of a log - any two minimal replays compatible with the log reach the same configuration.
informal.EventStructures.Trace.TraceMonoid: Defines the trace monoid as lists of events quotiented by the congruence generated by swapping adjacent concurrent events; paths in the configuration graph are quotiented by the same trace equivalence to form asynchronous paths.

records.title: Factorization Systems
records.abstract: Formalizes factorization systems, orthogonality, orthogonal complements, and the standard construction from weak factorization plus orthogonality.

informal.CategoryTheory.FactorizationSystem: Defines factorization systems on a category with specified left and right classes.
informal.CategoryTheory.FactorizationSystemCharac: Constructs a factorization system from repleteness, weak factorizations, and orthogonality.
informal.CategoryTheory.orthogonal: Defines orthogonality of two morphisms by existence and uniqueness of diagonal fillers.
informal.CategoryTheory.right_orthogonal_compleme: Defines the right orthogonal complement of a morphism property.

records.title: Fel's Conjecture on Syzygies of Numerical Semigroups
records.abstract: Formalizes Fel's conjectural formula for syzygies of numerical semigroups.

informal.fels_conjecture: Proves Fel's conjecture for the polynomial attached to numerical-semigroup syzygies.

records.title: FinEqs - reducing equations defining a subset of n-space over a finite field
records.abstract: Formalizes the finite-field equation-reduction theorem and sharpness examples.

informal.LeanPool.Fineqs.theorem_1: Reduces equations on a small finite set to at most n equations in the same span.
informal.LeanPool.Fineqs.prop_1: Shows the cardinality bound in the reduction theorem is sharp.
informal.LeanPool.Fineqs.corollary_2: Applies the reduction theorem to affine space over a finite field.
informal.LeanPool.Fineqs.corollary_3: Applies the reduction theorem to nonempty projective zero loci.
informal.LeanPool.Fineqs.remark_example: Shows n - 1 coordinate-function combinations have at least q common zeros.

records.title: Fundamental groups of finite connected graphs
records.abstract: Constructs the standard interval-cell realization of a finite connected directed multigraph and proves that its topological fundamental group is a free group of rank E - V + 1. The proof uses an explicit spanning-tree basis and develops a verified path-lifting cover, a contraction of the covering tree, root-change equivalences, the tree/triviality criterion, and the corresponding free-abelian result.

informal.FiniteGraphFreeGroup.graphTopologicalFun: For a finite weakly connected directed multigraph, the topological fundamental group of its interval-cell quotient realization at any vertex is explicitly isomorphic to the free group on E + 1 - V generators.
informal.FiniteGraphFreeGroup.graphCombinatorialT: The endomorphism group at a vertex in the graph's free groupoid is explicitly isomorphic to the topological fundamental group of the interval-cell realization.
informal.FiniteGraphFreeGroup.graphCoverProjectio: The canonical path-lifting projection from rooted free-groupoid paths to graph vertices is a quiver covering, with bijective maps on every incoming and outgoing edge star.
informal.FiniteGraphFreeGroup.graphRealization_tr: The interval-cell realization of a directed arborescence is simply connected, via an explicit continuous contraction to its root.
informal.FiniteGraphFreeGroup.graphFundamentalGro: The combinatorial fundamental group is trivial exactly when the graph's cycle rank E + 1 - V is zero.
The additive abelianization of the graph fundamental group is the free abelian group on E + 1 - V generators.

records.title: Sharp Five-Distance and Sup-Norm Gap Theorems
records.abstract: Formalizes sharp gap theorems for Kronecker sequences on tori: the Euclidean five-distance theorem on the 2-torus and the sup-norm gap bound, together with explicit arithmetic witnesses realizing the extremal cases - five distinct nearest-neighbour distances for the Euclidean and sup-norm metrics in dimension two, and nine distinct sup-norm distances in dimension three (Haynes-Marklof-Ramirez), via exact modular arithmetic on best simultaneous Diophantine approximations.

informal.ThreeGap.EuclideanRecords.sharp_attained: Exhibits a base point on the 2-torus with an irrational coordinate and an N whose Euclidean nearest-neighbour distances realize exactly five distinct values, showing the Euclidean five-distance bound is sharp.
informal.ThreeGap.LinftyRecords.sharp_attained: Exhibits a base point on the 2-torus with an irrational coordinate and an N whose sup-norm nearest-neighbour distances realize exactly five distinct values, showing the sup-norm gap bound is sharp in dimension two.
informal.ThreeGap.LinftyRecords3.nine_attained: Exhibits a base point on the 3-torus with an irrational coordinate and an N whose sup-norm nearest-neighbour distances realize at least nine distinct values, showing the sup-norm gap bound is sharp in dimension three.

records.title: The 5/8 theorem
records.abstract: Proves Gustafson's 5/8 theorem — the Mathlib commuting probability of a nonabelian group is at most 5/8, with the infinite case immediate from commProb being zero — via the finite-group index bounds for the center and centralizers of noncentral elements.

informal.FiveEighths.commProb_le_five_eighths: The commuting probability of a nonabelian group is at most 5/8.
informal.FiveEighths.centralFraction_le_quarter: The center of a finite nonabelian group contains at most a quarter of its elements.
informal.FiveEighths.centralizerFraction_le_half: The centralizer of a noncentral element of a finite group contains at most half of its elements.

records.title: Flean: Floating-Point Numbers in Lean
records.abstract: Formalizes a configurable model of floating-point numbers in Lean 4, including normal and subnormal representations, conversions between rationals and floats, round-trip correctness, and rounding error bounds.

informal.Flean.Float: Defines the floating-point number type parameterized by a precision and exponent configuration, with normal, subnormal, infinite, and NaN cases.
informal.toFloat: Rounds a rational number to the nearest representable floating-point value under a given rounding mode.
informal.toRat: Interprets a floating-point value as the exact rational number it represents.
informal.to_float_to_rat: Proves the round-trip identity that converting a finite nonzero float to a rational and back recovers the original float.
informal.roundf_close: Bounds the distance between a rational and its rounded floating-point representation.

records.title: First Order Language of ZF Set Theory
records.abstract: Formalizes ZF set theory inside Lean's `FirstOrder.Language` framework, enabling meta-mathematical arguments such as elementary submodels.

informal.FirstOrder.ZFC.ModelZF: Bundles the ZF axioms (Emptyset, Pairing, Union, Powerset, Infinity, Regularity, Comprehension, Replacement) into a single model class.
informal.FirstOrder.ZFC.ext_induction: States the principle of mathematical induction over ω externally for any bounded formula in LZFC.

records.title: Formal Learning Theory Kernel
records.abstract: Formalizes major equivalences and separations in PAC, VC, Gold-style, and online learning theory.

informal.vc_characterization: Characterizes PAC learnability by finite VC dimension.
informal.fundamental_theorem: Bundles the central PAC, VC, compression, Rademacher, and sample-complexity equivalences.
informal.fundamental_vc_compression: Relates finite VC dimension to compression with side information.
informal.gold_theorem: States the Gold-style characterization for identification in the limit.
informal.mind_change_characterization: Characterizes learnability by a bounded mind-change ordinal.
informal.littlestone_characterization: Characterizes online learnability by finite Littlestone dimension.
informal.pac_not_implies_online: Separates PAC learnability from online learnability.
informal.ex_not_implies_pac: Separates explanatory learnability from PAC learnability.

records.title: Strengthened V0 Bounded Arithmetic Interfaces
records.abstract: Formalizes first-order and two-sorted bounded-arithmetic model infrastructure, including arithmetic model laws and string-addition laws for strengthened bundled V0-style interfaces with propositional induction, order, cancellation, decidability, and algebraic laws assumed as fields rather than derived from a separate raw V0 class.

informal.IOPENModel.add_assoc: Proves associativity of addition in IOPEN models.
informal.IOPENModel.add_comm: Proves commutativity of addition in IOPEN models.
informal.IDelta0Model.pred_exists: Shows that nonzero elements in IDelta0 models have predecessors.
informal.IDelta0Model.mul_cancel_right: Proves right cancellation for multiplication by a nonzero element in IDelta0 models.
informal.V0Model.xind: Exposes string induction inside the strengthened bundled V0Model structure, whose fields include the comprehension and induction/order principles used downstream.
informal.V0Model.ind_strengthened_v0: Exposes propositional induction inside the strengthened bundled V0Model structure, rather than deriving it from only the raw finite V0 axiom list.
informal.str_add_comm_strengthened_v0: Proves commutativity of string addition in V0 extension models extending the strengthened V0Model bundle.
informal.str_add_assoc_strengthened_v0: Proves associativity of string addition in V0 extension models extending the strengthened V0Model bundle, using the bundled propositional induction field.
informal.str_succ_assoc_strengthened_v0: Proves that string addition associates with string successor in V0 extension models extending the strengthened V0Model bundle.

records.title: Forward Euler Method
records.abstract: Proves convergence of the explicit Euler method for ordinary differential equations.

informal.ODE.EulerMethod.dist_deriv_le: Bounds the local difference between the Euler derivative and the vector field along the Euler path.
informal.ODE.EulerMethod.dist_path_le: Bounds the distance between the Euler path and an exact solution using Gronwall's inequality.
informal.ODE.EulerMethod.tendsto_path: Proves that Euler paths converge pointwise to the true solution as the step size tends to zero from above.

records.title: Maxima of Coxeter frieze patterns are Fibonacci numbers
records.abstract: Formalizes the claim that the sequence of maxima of values of (Coxeter) arithmetic frieze patterns is the Fibonacci sequence, using a correspondence between arithmetic frieze patterns and n-flutes.

informal.main3: Proves that the maximum value of an arithmetic frieze pattern of width n is exactly the n-th Fibonacci number, and that this bound is attained.
informal.FluteBounded: Proves that every entry of an n-flute is bounded above by the n-th Fibonacci number.
informal.glideSymm: Proves the glide-reflection symmetry of Coxeter frieze patterns.
informal.translationInvariance: Proves the (n+1)-periodicity (horizontal translation invariance) of Coxeter frieze patterns.

records.title: FrontierMath Ramsey Hypergraphs
records.abstract: Formalizes lower bounds for the Brian-Larson hypergraph extremal function H(n), including a uniform 26/25 improvement over the recursive benchmark k_n for n ≥ 15 and a Lubell-frame asymptotic lower bound.

informal.HypergraphLowerBound.thm_main_H_lower_bo: Proves H(n) ≥ 26 * k(n) / 25 for every n ≥ 15.
informal.HypergraphLowerBound.uniform_26_25: Proves the uniform recursive construction bound A(n) ≥ 26 * k(n) / 25 for every n ≥ 15.
informal.HypergraphLowerBound.frame_recurrence: The substitution-frame recurrence that combines block witnesses and a valid support frame into a larger witness.
informal.HypergraphLowerBound.lubell_is_frame: Proves that the Lubell support family forms a valid frame for every arity t ≥ 2.
informal.HypergraphLowerBound.fixed_t_bound: Derives a fixed-t lower bound for the exact witness supremum from Lubell frames.
informal.HypergraphLowerBound.asymptotic_lower_bo: Proves the asymptotic lower bound liminf H(n) / k(n) ≥ 2 * log 2.
informal.HypergraphLowerBound.thm_asymptotic: States the asymptotic consequence in terms of H(n) divided by n log n.

records.title: The Fundamental Inequality of Valued Fields
records.abstract: Defines the ramification index and residue degree of an extension of valued fields and proves the fundamental inequality e * f ≤ finrank K L for finite extensions, via the valuation independence of products of coset representatives and residue-field basis lifts.

informal.Valuation.ramificationIndex: Defines the ramification index e(w/v) as the relative index of the value group of the restricted valuation inside the value group of the extension.
informal.Valuation.residueDegree: Defines the residue degree f(w/v) as the rank of the residue field extension.
informal.Valuation.valuation_independence: Elements with valuations in distinct cosets and residues that are linearly independent give products that are linearly independent over the base field.
informal.Valuation.fundamentalInequality: The fundamental inequality e(w/v) * f(w/v) ≤ finrank K L for finite extensions of valued fields.

records.title: Density-One GKP Divisibility and Its Carry-Language Characterization
records.abstract: Proves that the exponents k satisfying the Graham--Knuth--Patashnik divisibility condition have natural density one. The proof gives an exact all-depth modular sieve, quantitative bounds for possible failures in initial intervals, and a density-zero limit for the failure proportion. It also develops the Kummer digit-sum bridge, the binary-popcount reduction, and a verified ternary carry automaton. The universal GKP conjecture remains open because the possible density-zero failure set may be nonempty.

informal.GKPCarry.tendsto_gkpSuccessProportion_on: The proportion of exponents k below N for which nine divides the central binomial coefficient indexed by 2^k tends to one as N tends to infinity.
informal.GKPCarry.card_gkpFailureExponentsBelow_l: At each ternary depth n+3, the number of possible failures below N is at most (N divided by 2*3^(n+2), plus one) times (n+9)*2^n.
informal.GKPCarry.gkp_exact_modular_sieve: At depth n+3, exactly (n+9)*2^n of the 2*3^(n+2) exponent classes remain uncertified; every other class gives divisibility by nine and avoids the deficient carry language for all exponents in that class.
informal.GKPCarry.gkpConjecture_iff_badCarryLangu: The GKP conjecture is equivalent to the assertion that every nonexceptional power of two avoids the explicitly defined deficient-carry regular language. This is an exact reformulation and does not prove the remaining avoidance assertion.
informal.GKPCarry.nine_dvd_centralBinom_iff_two_l: For every natural number n, its central binomial coefficient is divisible by nine exactly when doubling the canonical ternary expansion of n creates at least two carries.
informal.GKPCarry.badCarryLanguage_true_iff_shape: The deficient-carry automaton accepts exactly three concrete little-endian ternary word shapes: all digits zero or one; a unique top digit two; or a unique two followed by a higher zero with all other digits zero or one.
informal.GKPCarry.card_badCarryWords: Among all ternary words of length n+2, exactly (n+7) times 2^n create fewer than two carries when doubled.
informal.GKPCarry.nine_dvd_centralBinom_four_pow_: For every m from 27 through 6560, nine divides the central binomial coefficient indexed by 4^m; this is a bounded computational corollary, not the headline result.

records.title: Grothendieck's Vanishing Theorem
records.abstract: Formalizes Grothendieck's vanishing theorem for sheaf cohomology on Noetherian topological spaces.

informal.GrothendieckVanishing: Proves vanishing of sheaf cohomology above the topological Krull dimension.
