records.title: rkirov/jordan_pick
records.abstract: The Jordan curve theorem, formalized in Lean 4 against Mathlib: a continuous injective map from the circle into the plane has a complement with exactly two connected components. The hypothesis is bare continuity and injectivity — no smoothness, piecewise-linearity or rectifiability — which is what makes the theorem hard and what separates it from the polygonal case. The proof follows Maehara's reduction to the Brouwer fixed point theorem, via a crossing lemma for transversal paths in a rectangle and the fact that every component has the curve as its boundary, together with a farthest-pair normalization that pins down exactly one bounded component. Because Mathlib has no Brouwer fixed point theorem at the pinned revision, Brouwer is built here from the ground up: covering-space path lifting for the circle giving π₁(S¹) ≅ ℤ, then no-retraction of the disk onto its boundary, then Brouwer on the disk by ray-retraction, then the general nonempty-compact-convex case by nearest-point projection. The statement is expressed in Mathlib's own vocabulary. The proof is sorry-free and depends on Lean's three standard axioms (propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound) and nothing else.

records.title: elliotglazer/erdos501
records.abstract: Erdős problem #501 (Erdős 1961; Erdős–Hajnal 1971, Problem 38): for every real x let A_x be a bounded set of reals of Lebesgue outer measure < 1; must there be an infinite independent set, i.e. an infinite X ⊆ ℝ with x ∉ A_y for all distinct x, y ∈ X?  And if the sets A_x are closed of measure < 1, must there be an independent set of size 3?  This repository formalizes both answers.  Second question: yes — closed sets of measure < 1 admit an infinite independent set (Newelski–Pawlikowski–Seredyński 1987; no boundedness is needed), hence one of size 3.  First question: independent of ZFC.  Under CH (as ℵ₁ = 𝔠) Hechler's 1972 construction gives a family of bounded sets of outer measure < 1 (in fact countable and null) with no infinite independent set — a Mathlib-level theorem — and the negation of the first question holds in the Boolean-valued model of the collapse algebra Col(ω₁, 𝒫(ω)); after adding 𝔠⁺ random reals (Glazer and Sol 2026, adapting the paper's ω₂ random reals over a CH ground) the first question has a positive answer, so it holds in the Boolean-valued model of the random algebra with 𝔠⁺ coordinates.  Both Boolean-valued models are built in a Lean 4 port of Han–van Doorn's Flypitch (the framework of their independence-of-CH proof), and Flypitch's completeness theorem turns them into two-valued models.  The comparator challenge states the results in Mathlib alone: the language of set theory, the theory ZFC (Flypitch's axiomatization: extensionality, empty set, ordered pairs, union, power set, infinity, regularity, Zorn's lemma, strong collection) and the sentence Erdos501 ("every complete ordered field has the Erdős property") are defined in Mathlib's ModelTheory, and independence is stated semantically as ¬ (ZFC ⊨ᵇ Erdos501) ∧ ¬ (ZFC ⊨ᵇ ∼Erdos501); a faithfulness theorem shows that in Mathlib's ZFSet the sentence is equivalent to the Mathlib statement of the first question, verbatim the proposition of google-deepmind/formal-conjectures.  All targets are proved from propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound only.  As far as we know this is the first Erdős problem whose resolution is a formally verified independence result.

records.title: WillWhistler/Regts-Sevenster
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the Regts–Sevenster conjecture, proved in both directions and resting on no assumption. A complex-valued graph parameter that is normalized at the empty graph and invariant under isomorphism has exponentially bounded edge-connection rank if and only if it is the partition function of a mixed edge-colouring model; and when the rank base is R the model may be taken with k even and ℓ odd colours satisfying k, 2ℓ ≤ ⌊2eR⌋. Nothing is assumed. Deligne's theorem on tensor categories, on which the forward direction rests, is itself proved in the development — in the fibre-functor form that is the substance of Deligne's own proof, and by a route through simple algebras in the ind-completion rather than his descent argument — and each of its hypotheses is discharged for a concretely constructed rigid symmetric monoidal envelope of the parameter's skein category. The symmetric-group character theory the argument needs is proved from Mathlib's linear algebra rather than cited, and the converse direction reproves Regts and Sevenster's own theorem. Every theorem of record depends only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound, pinned in-tree so that a change to the axiom set is a build failure rather than a review task.

records.title: stalex444/pdt-lean
records.abstract: Kernel-checked exact-constant results for the CHSH operator T = A₀B₀ + A₀B₁ + A₁B₀ − A₁B₁ of an arbitrary CHSH tuple (Mathlib's IsCHSHTuple: self-adjoint involutions with the A's commuting with the B's). (1) The Landau identity: in any *-ring, T² = 4 + [A₀,A₁]·[B₁,B₀] — the exact, representation-independent correction to the naive T² = 8·1 (chsh_mul_self). (2) Tsirelson's bound in norm form: ‖T‖ ≤ 2√2 for every CHSH tuple in every nontrivial unital real C*-normed algebra (chsh_norm_le). (3) The classical constant, exactly: if either party's pair commutes, ‖T‖ = 2 — not merely ≤ 2 (chsh_norm_of_comm). (4) Necessity of noncommutativity: any violation ‖T‖ > 2 forces A₀A₁ ≠ A₁A₀ and B₀B₁ ≠ B₁B₀ — noncommutativity within both parties is necessary for any violation of the classical bound (noncomm_of_chsh_norm_gt_two). (5) The exact constant of M₄(ℝ): in the l2 operator norm, 2√2 is the greatest element of the set of CHSH operator norms over 4×4 real matrices — an upper bound for every tuple, attained by an explicit real-Pauli tuple (chsh_opNorm_isGreatest), so the maximal violation 2√2 is possible, not just bounded. The witness side stays compared: the explicit quadruple is verified to be a genuine CHSH tuple, its CHSH operator has eigenvalue exactly 2√2 on the explicit nonzero vector (1,0,0,1) and l2 operator norm exactly 2√2; the ordered star-ring bounds T ≤ (2√2)·1 and (commutative case) T ≤ 2 and the strict gap 2 < 2√2 complete the picture. A falsification is compared alongside: the saturating tuple's T² is not c·1 for ANY real c (chsh_sq_ne quantifies over every scalar), so the scalar-square route to the norm is closed for every scalar; the norm results here go through the C*-identity (and, for the generic bound, the Landau identity) instead.

records.title: yuanchenyang/lean_low_rank_univariate_sos
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the main theorem of Legat, Yuan and Parrilo, "Low-Rank Univariate Sum of Squares Has No Spurious Local Minima" (SIAM J. Optim. 33(3), 2023). For a real univariate polynomial p and a pair of polynomials u = (u₁, u₂), consider the quadratically penalized Burer–Monteiro objective f_p(u) = ‖σ(u) - p‖² with σ(u) = u₁² + u₂², the norm coming from any inner product on ℝ[x]. The formalized theorem states that if p is a sum of two squares (which is the case for any nonnegative  univariate polynomial) and u is a second-order critical point of f_p (vanishing gradient and positive semidefinite Hessian, Definition 3.1 of the paper), then σ(u) = p, equivalently f_p(u) = 0; hence every SOCP, and in particular every local minimum, is a global minimum. The development follows the paper's proof: the gcd decomposition u = a·u₀ with u₀ coprime, the observation that σ(u₀) has no real roots, a Bézout-based "hgroup" lemma writing a sum of squares p as g·q + s·σ(u₀) with s a sum of squares when g and σ(u₀) are coprime, the factor-peeling argument that replaces the quadratic factors of a shared with σ(u₀) by X², and the final certificate argument combining the first- and second-order conditions.

records.title: catskillsresearch/cardb
records.abstract: A Lean formalization of an exact enumeration identity and two consequences: for a finite type α, the number of families B ⊆ Set α that are topological bases equals the sum, over all topologies τ on α, of 2^(|τ| − |M_τ|), where M_τ is the canonical minimal basis of minimal open neighbourhoods (Mathlib's nhdsKer {x} at each point). Kernel-reducible enumeration gives the exact table #(0)=2, #(1)=2, #(2)=10, #(3)=142. A quantitative sandwich then shows that the discrete fiber 2^(2^N − N) dominates: for N ≥ 2 the remaining fibers contribute at most 2^(N(N−1) + 3·2^(N−2)), the ratio to the discrete term tends to 1, and for N ≥ 10 the total is at most twice the discrete term. The argument is a fiber decomposition: every finite topology is Alexandrov-discrete, the minimal neighbourhoods generate it, and the bases generating τ are exactly the families B with M_τ ⊆ B ⊆ {U | τ.IsOpen U}. The informal account is the companion note CARDB.md in this repository. The Lean source was written by AI agents under the direction and review of the author. records.title: google-deepmind/formal-conjectures
records.abstract: Formal proof of the First Cuboid Conjecture, which states that for all positive coprime integers a, b with a ≠ b, a certain degree-8 polynomial P_{a,b}(t) over ℤ is irreducible. This conjecture was proposed by Shapirov in "Perfect cuboids and irreducible polynomials" (arXiv:1108.5348) as part of a family of three conjectures whose combined truth would imply the nonexistence of a perfect Euler brick. The proof first analyses rational factors and the symmetry F(−x) vs F(x) to reduce irreducibility of the degree-8 polynomial to irreducibility of a degree-4 factor Q_{a,b}, and the coprime branch to a Diophantine identity. Irreducibility of Q is in turn reduced to the quartic Diophantine equation x⁴ + 34x²y² + y⁴ = z², whose only trivial solutions are established by Fermat-style infinite descent. The formal proof was autonomously discovered by the AlphaProof Nexus agent; an independent informal proof using rank-zero elliptic curves was given by Asiryan (arXiv:2510.11768).

records.title: rwst/Even-Integral
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib development of a paper, which improves on a problem by Dubickas. Dubickas (Glasgow Math. J. 48 (2006), 331–336) splits the reals α > 1 in two: α lies in 𝒵 when some real ξ ≠ 0 makes every integral part ⌊ξαⁿ⌋, n ≥ 1, even, and in 𝒮 otherwise. At α = 3/2 this is Mahler's question, and open; his Problem 5 asks whether 𝒮 has an element greater than 2. This formalization decides 𝒮 versus 𝒵 for every quadratic Pisot number: the golden mean is the only one in 𝒮, so none greater than 2 lies there and Problem 5 loses its whole natural class of candidates, though the problem itself stays open. The case that had resisted the source paper's four constructions is α = 1 + √2, settled by an exact computation rather than an estimate: with ξ = (2−√2)/4 one has ⌊ξ(1+√2)^(n+1)⌋ = Pₙ − [n odd] for the Pell numbers P, so every integral part is even. The mechanism generalizes: for a real quadratic pair with second conjugate in (−1,0), the closed-form multiplier ξ = −β/(α−β) makes m divide ⌊ξαⁿ⌋ for every n ≥ 0 whenever m ∣ a and m ∣ b−1 — an exact congruence, not a confinement of fractional parts — and all but finitely many of those integral parts are then composite. The informal account is the companion paper doi:10.13140/RG.2.2.20582.79689. Credit divides as follows, in contributor terms rather than bibliographic ones: the mathematical discovery and the formalization are the AI agent's; the agent also drafted the prose of the companion paper, which the author revised; the direction and the review are the author's, who is responsible for the mathematical content. Bibliographic authorship of the paper is the author's alone — the agent is credited in its Acknowledgements, not in its byline, as is usual for an AI tool. records.title: sloisel/MPE-Formal
records.abstract: Machine-checked proofs of three probabilistic convergence theorems for restarted Minimal Polynomial Extrapolation (MPE) applied to nonlinear fixed-point iterations.  Dithered restarts keep the error below the doubly exponential schedule delta^(theta^m), for any theta in (1,2), from every starting point -- the breakdown set included -- with an explicit failure-probability exponent over the dither; in the root sense the convergence order is at least theta.  Under simple spectrum, the error follows a quadratically shrinking dither schedule (root order at least 2) with failure probability linear in the initial radius up to a logarithmic factor, and MPE coincides with Reduced Rank Extrapolation at every cycle. With no dither at all, the restarted iteration from a single uniformly random starting point at worst squares the error at every cycle with high probability, under two checkable hypotheses on the Jacobian and the quadratic Taylor coefficients.  The registered statements are self-contained over mathlib: every object of the construction is introduced by an explicit defining equation among the hypotheses.

records.title: ehrlich-b/sequential-products-lean
records.abstract:
A sequential product on the effects of an order-unit space is a binary operation a & b, read "first test a, then test b with the state updated by the first test", satisfying the seven axioms S1-S7 of van de Wetering (arXiv:1803.11139, Definition 2). This development registers two classification theorems for such products on the Hermitian matrix algebras.
On H_N(R), the Hermitian N x N real matrices with N >= 1, every sequential product is the Lueders product sqrt(a) b sqrt(a): there is no free parameter. On H_N(C) with N >= 3, every sequential product has the twist normal form a^(1/2+it) b a^(1/2-it) for a unique real t. The twist family is a one-parameter deformation of the Lueders product, and the complex theorem says nothing outside it satisfies the axioms. The equations are asserted on all effects, including singular ones, and the uniqueness of t is part of the registered statement.
Direction. Both registered classification theorems are necessity: a product satisfying the axioms is supplied, and the theorem says it has the stated normal form. The two converses differ in status and neither is registered. For the complex case, that each real t defines a SeqProd satisfying S2 is proved in the wider development; together with the registered uniqueness it is what would make the parameter map injective. For the real case, that the Lueders formula defines a SeqProd satisfying S2 is not proved anywhere in this development. Nothing here registers a bijection between parameters and products, or the admissibility of the Lueders formula.
The package also registers two classical theorems the development proves in passing. Albert's power-associativity theorem: in a commutative Jordan ring carrying an R-module structure, x^(m+1) * x^(n+1) = x^(m+n+2), with no unit, finite dimension, formal reality or positivity assumed. And the real case of Wigner's theorem: every transition probability preserving self-map of the rays of a finite-dimensional real inner product space is induced by a linear isometry, with bijectivity not assumed but derived.
Both classification theorems are proved from S1-S7 with no hypotheses beyond the dimension bounds, and their axiom closures contain only Lean's three core axioms (propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound). The continuity axiom S2 is stated in the order-unit norm, as an explicit epsilon-delta condition, so the statement file depends on no normed-space or topological instance; the equivalence with continuity in the carrier's Frobenius topology is proved in the development.
Scope. Comparator registers four theorems across three separate entries: the two sequential-product classifications above, which use the SeqProd interface and the axiom S2 and correspond to numbered rows of the manuscript; and the two ancillary classical theorems, Albert and Wigner, which use neither and correspond to no manuscript row. Nothing beyond those four registered theorems is claimed by this submission.
The two classification theorems are two rows of a thirty-six row manifest tracking the numbered results of the accompanying manuscript. The manuscript as a whole is not formalized: as of 2026-08-12 the manifest stands at 12 rows formalized, 19 partial, and 5 absent. In particular the quaternionic row H_n(H) and the Albert-algebra row H_3(O) of the manuscript's main theorem are not proved here, and the coalescence and diagonal-homomorphism lemmas are established on the concrete carrier H_N(C) rather than at the manuscript's stated generality of a finite-dimensional simple Euclidean Jordan algebra.

records.title: teal-sea/zeta-lab
records.abstract: A variational identity for the Fredholm operator A = I + T on the interval I = [-1/2, 1/2], where T is convolution against the Farmer-Gonek-Lee pair-correlation form factor F1(x) = |x| - 4x^2 + sum_k a_k |x|^(2k+3) with a_k = 2^(2k+3) k! / (2k+2)!. Let w = A^(-1)1 and c* = <1, A^(-1)1>. Over the source-admissible class of scalar profiles v(s) = phi(Ls)^2 induced by even, radially nonincreasing C^2 windows supported exactly on [-L/2, L/2] with 0 <= phi <= 1 and uniform L^1 bounds on phi'' and (phi^2)'', the supremum of <1,v>^2 / <Av,v> equals c*, and the infimum of the reciprocal quotient <Av,v> / <1,v>^2 equals 1/c*. The upper bound <1,v>^2 <= c* <Av,v> is energy Cauchy-Schwarz. It holds for every v, it is classical, and it is not the content of this result. The content is the reverse inequality over the constrained class: c* is the value of the unconstrained variational problem, and the identity says that imposing evenness, radial monotonicity, an exact compact support, the amplitude ceiling 0 <= phi <= 1 and uniform L^1 bounds on the second derivatives does not lower the supremum. That direction is proved by exhibiting an explicit endpoint-tapered family inside the class, indexed by the scale L, whose quotient converges to c*. Both orientations are advertised because the orientation is load-bearing: it is the quotient with <1,v>^2 in the numerator whose supremum is c*, and the supporting development also proves that the two are not interchangeable. The advertised statement is existential in the profile and in the two uniform constants, so it carries its own non-vacuity: an IsLUB or IsGLB assertion over the image of an empty class is unsatisfiable in the reals, so the theorem cannot hold unless the class is populated by the constants for which it is stated. Audience. The kernel F1 is the pair-correlation form factor and the window class is the generalized, load-bearing class of Section 7.1 of the cited paper rather than a convenient flat-topped realization, so the constrained supremum settled here is the quantity that a critical-line proportion argument built on that framework optimizes; analytic number theorists working on the proportion of zeros of the Riemann zeta function on the critical line, and on pair correlation of its zeros, are the audience for which the exact value of that supremum over the admissible class, rather than a bound on it, is the relevant fact. The statement is also a closure result for a constrained admissible class in the variational theory of Fredholm integral operators (MSC 45B05, 49R05) and can be read there without reference to its origin. What the theorem itself asserts is bounded by the scope field below: it is a statement about a Fredholm operator on an interval and a class of test profiles, and it is evidence for nothing beyond that.

records.title: teal-sea/zeta-lab
records.abstract: Davenport and Heilbronn (1936) exhibited a Dirichlet series with real coefficients satisfying a Riemann-type functional equation which nevertheless has zeros off the critical line. It is the standard demonstration that a functional equation of Riemann type does not on its own force the Riemann Hypothesis, it is the reference counterexample against which structural explanations of the Riemann Hypothesis are tested, and the location of its zeros remains an active subject. The function is DH(s) = (1 - i*kappa)/2 * L(s, chi) + (1 + i*kappa)/2 * L(s, chi^-1) for a quartic Dirichlet character chi mod 5 and kappa = (sqrt(10 - 2*sqrt 5) - 2)/(sqrt 5 - 1), the value that rotates the two conjugate root numbers onto each other and so makes the Dirichlet coefficients real. This submission advertises one theorem, the analytic half of the Davenport-Heilbronn theorem: there exists an entire function represented by the Davenport-Heilbronn Dirichlet series on Re z > 1 whose completion (pi/5)^(-(s+1)/2) * Gamma((s+1)/2) * f(s) is symmetric under s -> 1-s. The statement is existential in f, so it carries its own non-vacuity and needs none of the character theory used to construct the witness. What the work consists of. The Davenport-Heilbronn function is not a library object anywhere we could find, so the development builds it: the quartic character mod 5, the linear combination, entirety on all of C, the identification of the Dirichlet coefficients as the real period-5 sequence 1, kappa, -kappa, -1, 0, and the completed functional equation. The last of these is where the content sits. It reduces to a root-number identity whose convention-sensitive constants are derived inside the development, from Mathlib's Real.cos_pi_div_five by radical algebra, rather than transcribed from a table; the standard sources state kappa without deriving it in a form a kernel will accept, and getting it wrong yields a function whose coefficients are not real and which therefore is not the counterexample. The functional equation is stated with explicit guards excluding the poles of the two Gamma factors, because Mathlib's junk value Gamma = 0 at the poles would otherwise make the unrestricted equation false for reasons having nothing to do with the mathematics. The Davenport-Heilbronn function is a named object of analytic number theory with a continuing literature on its zeros, so a machine-checked construction of it is of direct interest to number theorists working on zeros of L-functions and on what a Riemann-type functional equation does and does not imply. A search of Mathlib at the revision pinned by this repository found no Davenport-Heilbronn function and no formalization of this functional equation. That is a bounded search of one library. No systematic search of other proof assistants or of the mathematical literature for prior formalizations has been run, and no novelty against the literature is claimed: the mathematics is Davenport and Heilbronn's, published in 1936. Its full statement additionally requires a zero s with Re s different from 1/2, and that conjunct appears nowhere in the advertised theorem. What is offered is the analytic half alone. records.title: adas1236/KaltonPeckPalomar
records.abstract:
We prove the following mod-2 identity for real symplectic Banach spaces:
  If $(X, \omega)$ is a real symplectic Banach space, and $T \in L(X)$ satisfies:
    (1) $I + T^+T$ is Fredholm
    (2) $I + T^2$ has finite rank
  Then
    $\rank(T^2 + I) \equiv \dim \ker (I + T^+T) \pmod 2$.
In the above, $T^+$ represents the symplectic adjoint. See our paper for more depth in definitions. This identity is applied to show that no hyperplane of the real Kalton-Peck space has a complex structure. We note that in our notation, a symplectic Banach space always assumes that the symplectic form \omega is a strong symplectic form. See our paper for more detail on the definitions.
We formalize:
 (1) The mod-2 identity for arbitrary real symplectic Banach spaces
 (2) An application of the identity to show that if $T \in L(Z_2)$ and $T^2 + I$ has finite rank, then $T^2 + I$ has even rank.
     Here, Z_2 is the real Kalton-Peck space.
 (3) The corollary that no hyperplane of the real Kalton-Peck space has a complex structure.

records.title: CBirkbeck/uniform-sheafy-tate-domains-lean
records.abstract:
A Lean 4 formalisation of *Uniform sheafy Tate rings that are not stably uniform* (Birkbeck–Torzewski), answering Question 7 of Kedlaya's *Nonarchimedean Scottish Book* in the negative: a sheafy uniform Huber pair need not be stably uniform. Buzzard–Verberkmoes and Mihara proved that stably uniform Tate Huber rings are sheafy; whether the converse holds was open.
The paper gives two complete Tate algebras over a complete discretely valued field `k` that are uniform, nonnoetherian integral domains with `A° = A₀`, strongly sheafy (every Tate algebra `A⟨X₁, …, Xₙ⟩` is sheafy), and yet not stably uniform, because an explicit rational localisation is not uniform. The first (Theorem 1.1) is the finite-jet pinching algebra `𝓐 = B ×_D C`, the pullback of a Milnor square with `B = k⟨W, Q⟩/(Q²)`, `C = k⟨W, W⁻¹⟩⟨Q⟩`, `D = C/(Q²)` — concretely, the series in `k⟨W, W⁻¹⟩⟨Q⟩` whose `Q⁰`- and `Q¹`-coefficients have nonnegative `W`-support; its bad chart `𝓐⟨W/ϖ⟩ ≅ k⟨X, Q⟩/(Q²)` is non-reduced. The second (Theorem 8.1) is the weighted-parity algebra `𝒜_w`, whose bad chart is an integral domain; the paper proves it for every unbounded weight `w ≥ 1`, the formalisation for `w(n) = n`.
This submission certifies the seven conclusions of Theorem 1.1 together with two statements ruling out a vacuous reading of its sheafiness claims, stated self-containedly on Mathlib in `Challenge.lean` over an arbitrary complete ultrametric field with DVR valuation ring; Theorem 8.1 is certified by the repository's in-library configuration. The repository also develops the surrounding theory after Wedhorn's *Adic Spaces*: Huber and Tate rings, the adic spectrum, rational localisations, the structure presheaf, and sheafiness (Definition 8.26), including the strongly noetherian theorem (8.28(b)).

records.title: geoconuk/lean-misc-math
records.abstract: For a fixed angular radius theta in (0, pi/2), the least number M(n, theta) of spherical caps of angular radius theta, centred at points of the unit sphere of R^n, whose union is that whole sphere satisfies (1/n) log M(n, theta) -> -log sin theta as n -> infinity. This is the covering half of Wyner (1967): the elementary volume bound gives the lower bound on the covering number and a random-covering argument gives the upper bound. The statement is given in Mathlib's own vocabulary, as an asymptotic for Metric.coveringNumber of Metric.sphere 0 1 in EuclideanSpace R (Fin n) at chordal radius 2 sin (theta/2), and introduces no definition of its own; two compared lemmas establish that an angular cap of half-angle theta about a unit vector is exactly the closed chordal ball of that radius, which is what licenses reading the result as a statement about caps. Two further compared theorems rule out the junk values that the N-infinity-valued covering number and the logarithm would otherwise admit.

records.title: rwst/Square-Roots
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib development of a paper, which answers a problem by Dubickas. Dubickas (Glasgow Math. J. 48 (2006), 331–336) splits the reals α > 1 in two: α lies in 𝒵 when some real ξ ≠ 0 makes every integral part ⌊ξαⁿ⌋, n ≥ 1, even, and in 𝒮 otherwise. At α = 3/2 this is Mahler's question, and open; his Problem 3 asks whether √3 lies in 𝒮 or in 𝒵. This formalization settles that question and the whole square-root slice: √3 ∈ 𝒵 by an explicit ξ = 1.34160899796…, and for an integer m ≥ 2 one has √m ∈ 𝒮 exactly when m = 2. The cells √5, √6, √7, √8 put four explicit points of 𝒵 in the interval (2,3), the only interval where an answer to Dubickas's Problem 5 could live; they are formalized (SZ.exists_mem_MahlerZ_Ioo_two_three) but are not separately compared, being subsumed by the compared Theorem B. The mechanism is not Diophantine approximation but the arithmetic of Cantor sets, and rests on the triviality that √m² = m is an integer: splitting n into even and odd values turns the one orbit into two base-m orbits coupled by x + √m y = σ, and a covering induction — Utz's 1951 theorem on the distance set of the Cantor discontinuum at m = 3, proved here for every base and every modulus — solves that equation inside the restricted-digit set. The same machinery at a general modulus gives, for p ≥ 2 and non-square m ≥ 3 in either of two explicit ranges, a real ξ ≠ 0 with p ∣ ⌊ξ√mⁿ⌋ for every n ≥ 1, hence integral parts that are composite from some point on; and the greedy's branching shows the witnesses for √3 have cardinality 2^ℵ₀, so all but countably many of them are transcendental. The informal account is the companion paper doi:10.13140/RG.2.2.32215.43682. records.title: ehrlich-b/euclidean-jordan
records.abstract:
A Euclidean Jordan algebra is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space carrying a commutative bilinear product with a unit, satisfying the Jordan identity (x*y)*(x*x) = x*(y*(x*x)) and the associativity of the inner product <x*y, z> = <y, x*z>. This is Faraut-Koranyi's definition (Analysis on Symmetric Cones, III.1). This development formalizes the classical structure theory of these algebras.
Mathlib carries the Jordan identity as the typeclass IsCommJordan together with five operator-commutation lemmas, and nothing beyond that: no idempotent theory, no Peirce decomposition, no spectral theory. This development supplies that layer.
The registered results, in four separate Comparator configurations. (1) The Koecher / Alfsen-Shultz theorem: a unital linear order isomorphism of a Euclidean Jordan algebra is a Jordan automorphism, with the cone taken to be the sums-of-squares cone and the product carried as a bundled bilinear map so that the statement needs no ring instance to elaborate. (2) The single-element spectral theorem: every element of a finite-dimensional formally real Jordan algebra is a real linear combination of a complete family of pairwise-orthogonal idempotents. Finite-dimensionality is load-bearing rather than decorative - the polynomial algebra R[X] satisfies every other hypothesis and has no nonconstant spectral resolution. (3) The Jordan trace form tau(x,y) = tr(L_{x*y}): symmetric, associative, and positive definite, constructed from the multiplication alone rather than assumed. Symmetry and associativity are registered at their honest generality, which does not include finite-dimensionality; positive definiteness needs the spectral theorem and therefore does. (4) The frame Peirce decomposition: for a Jordan frame p_1, ..., p_n the algebra is the internal direct sum of the blocks V_ij over unordered pairs, together with the Faraut-Koranyi table entry dim V_ii = 1.
Direction and scope. Every registered theorem is proved outright from the stated hypotheses; none is conditional on a cited result. The development also proves, but does not register here, Albert's power-associativity theorem (x^(m+1) * x^(n+1) = x^(m+n+2), with no unit, finite dimension, formal reality or positivity assumed), which is registered from a separate development of the author's and is deliberately not re-registered; the existence of a Jordan frame in any nontrivial finite-dimensional Euclidean Jordan algebra; the associativity of the subalgebra generated by a single element; the Peirce subalgebras J_2(c) and J_0(c) as Euclidean Jordan algebras in their own right; and an order-unit-space structure with the sums-of-squares cone, proved to coincide with the Loewner order on the concrete carrier.
What is NOT here. Coordinatization is absent: the Jordan-von Neumann-Wigner route continues by making the off-diagonal block a composition algebra and applying Hurwitz's theorem to land J = H_n(K), and that step depends on the composition-algebra classification, which lives in a separate repository. This development therefore stops at the connectors and the frame-block structure. There is no functional calculus on the spectral resolution. Frame conjugacy (Faraut-Koranyi IV.2.5) is not proved - the development sidesteps it by carrying a Jordan frame as data rather than reasoning about the rank as a number. The classification of simple Euclidean Jordan algebras is not proved, and no statement about the exceptional algebra H_3(O) appears. Formal reality and the associativity of the inner product are equivalent over R in finite dimension, but that equivalence is not formalized, so both appear as hypotheses.
The abstract theory has a live carrier: H_n(K) for K = R or C, the Hermitian matrices under A*B = (AB+BA)/2, is an instance of the EuclideanJordanAlgebra class, checked by instance synthesis in the mechanical audit rather than by inspection. The check is finer than nonemptiness of the class: every Peirce rule mentioning the half-eigenspace would be vacuously true on a carrier where that space is trivial, and it is trivial for the two idempotents one reaches for first, so a witness with nonzero half-eigenspace is exhibited on H_2(C).
Every declaration in the tracked tree has an axiom closure contained in Lean's three core axioms (propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound). The tree carries no custom axiom, no sorry and no native_decide.

Frame conjugacy (Faraut-Koranyi IV.2.5) is not proved - the development sidesteps it by carrying a Jordan frame as data rather than reasoning about the rank as a number. The classification of simple Euclidean Jordan algebras is not proved, and no statement about the exceptional algebra H_3(O) appears. Formal reality and the associativity of the inner product are equivalent over R in finite dimension, but that equivalence is not formalized, so both appear as hypotheses.
The abstract theory has a live carrier: H_n(K) for K = R or C, the Hermitian matrices under A*B = (AB+BA)/2, is an instance of the EuclideanJordanAlgebra class, checked by instance synthesis in the mechanical audit rather than by inspection. The check is finer than nonemptiness of the class: every Peirce rule mentioning the half-eigenspace would be vacuously true on a carrier where that space is trivial, and it is trivial for the two idempotents one reaches for first, so a witness with nonzero half-eigenspace is exhibited on H_2(C).
Every declaration in the tracked tree has an axiom closure contained in Lean's three core axioms (propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound). The tree carries no custom axiom, no sorry and no native_decide.

records.abstract: Let N(T,2T) count the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function with ordinate in (T,2T], with multiplicity, and N_0^s(T,2T) the simple zeros among them on the critical line. The Lean development accompanying arXiv:2608.13637 (anthropics/zeta-23-lean) proves, for Mathlib's riemannZeta and unconditionally, that for every eps > 0 and all large T, (H - eps) N(T,2T) <= N_0^s(T,2T), with H = 3/2 - (1/sqrt 2) cot(1/sqrt 2) = 0.67250070367941164573... (its Theorem D). Ainta (github.com/ainta/zeta-simple-zeros) refines H by carrying the spectral defect of the Gram matrix of the simple-zero vectors through that argument and bounding it block by block through a local inequality on seven points. Advertised here: that refinement carried out for n points at once, and three instances. Parametrically, for n >= 2, c > 0, m >= n, p > 0 with c(m-(n-1)) <= 1, if c <= F(n,p,g) for every nonnegative vector g of n-1 gaps (the hypothesis hCert), then for every eps > 0 and all large T, (Phi_n(n,c,m,p) - eps) N(T,2T) <= N_0^s(T,2T), where Phi_n(n,c,m,p) = (H - (n-1)(m-1)/(pm)) / (1 - c(m-(n-1))/m). At n = 7 this is Ainta's theorem. THE THREE-POINT INSTANCE IS UNCONDITIONAL. At (n,c,p) = (3, 1345/10^6, 3000) the hypothesis is proved, not assumed: the overlap weight w = k^2 is enclosed from a twelve-term Taylor bound on cos and sin and the closed form of the kernel, and 368 interval cell lemmas over rationals, applied 1515 times over 487 leaves, cover the quarter-plane of the two gaps. No external interval-arithmetic certificate is assumed for the three-point theorem, and no floating point appears. The cap gives m = 745 and the constant (149000000 H - 99200)/148800133 = 0.67273733450380945875..., exceeding H by 2.3663e-4: for Mathlib's riemannZeta, an unconditional improvement of the dependency's Theorem D. THE FOUR-POINT INSTANCE IS ALSO UNCONDITIONAL. At (n,c,p) = (4, 2310/10^6, 2500), the finite inequality at every triple of nonnegative gaps is proved inside Lean. The cap gives m = 435 and the resulting constant is (906250 H - 1085)/904171 = 0.67284701976668870316.... The bound and ratio carry no certificate hypothesis and use exactly the same three permitted axioms. The eight-point instance stays conditional. Our n-point generalisation of Ainta's interval verifier accepts c = 41763/10^7 at p = 3200, giving m = 246 and 0.67305298298962888...; interval-arithmetic acceptance is not a Lean proof, so hCert remains explicit. records.title: JaTaSn/lattice-line-covers
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of Theorem 1 of arXiv:2608.22550: there is a family of lattice lines covering the integer plane whose set of realized directions is dense. Concretely, a family F of subsets of Z^2 is exhibited such that (i) every member is a genuine lattice line, the nonempty solution set of Px + Qy = c with P, Q coprime; (ii) the members cover Z^2; (iii) two members of different direction are disjoint, so no lattice point is covered twice in different directions; and (iv) the directions that occur are dense in the space RP^1 of line directions, that is, every angle in [0, pi) is approximated to within any epsilon by the direction of some member. The construction is recursive and works on nested regions: a chain of cosets Z^2 = R_0 > R_1 > R_2 > ... is built, and at stage k the region R_k is partitioned into sub-cosets of a new coprime direction, one of which is reserved to become R_{k+1} while lines of that direction claim all the others. Coverage is what the choice of reserved sub-coset is for: fix a surjective enumeration z_0, z_1, ... of Z^2 and reserve, at stage k, a sub-coset that does not contain z_k -- always possible, since the partition has at least four sub-cosets and only the one containing z_k must be avoided. Every point is then claimed: it is z_k for some k, and either it had already left the region at an earlier stage, in which case the coverage invariant Z^2 \ R_k = union over i < k of (R_i \ R_{i+1}) shows it was claimed there, or it is still in R_k and the reservation rule places it in a sub-coset claimed at stage k. Reserving an arbitrary sub-coset would not do: without that diagonal choice a point could survive in every R_k and never be claimed. Disjointness is a consequence of that partition rather than of any criterion for when two individual lines meet: distinct sub-cosets of a region are disjoint, each stage's lines stay inside the sub-cosets they claim, and the regions claimed at distinct stages are therefore disjoint. Earlier lines survive untouched because everything a later stage touches lies inside the reserved region. Only Theorem 1 is formalized; the paper's further remarks and discussion are not.

records.title: g-pichler/bsc-averaging
records.abstract:
A Lean 4 / Mathlib development that settles three previously open problems about
binary channels on a doubly symmetric binary source (DSBS): a pair (X, Y) of Bernoulli(1/2)
bits with P(X != Y) = p, together with Markov chains U - X - Y - V in which U and V are the
outputs of two independent binary channels applied to X and to Y. All quantities are in nats.

(1) MathOverflow 285151, "Do averaged binary symmetric channels maximize mutual information?"
(Georg Pichler, 2017; unanswered there) asks whether conv A = conv B, where A is the set of
rate triples (R0, R1, R2) with I(U;X) <= R1, I(Y;V) <= R2 and R0 <= I(U;V) attainable by
arbitrary binary channels on the two sides, and B is the same set with both channels
restricted to be binary symmetric. The inclusion B subset A is elementary; the question is
whether taking convex hulls closes the gap, which the counterexample to the predecessor
question MathOverflow 213084 leaves open. This development proves conv A = conv B for every
p in [0,1] (`averaged_bsc_maximise_mutual_information`). The same statement settles
Conjecture 5.2 of Pichler, Piantanida and Matz, "Distributed Information-Theoretic
Clustering", Information and Inference 11 (2022) 1029-1082.

(2), (3) Conjectures 1 and 2 of Dikshtein, Ordentlich and Shamai (Shitz), "The Double-Sided
Information Bottleneck Function", Entropy 24(9):1321 (2022), which concern the double-sided
information bottleneck function R(Cu, Cv) = max I(U;V) subject to I(X;U) <= Cu and
I(Y;V) <= Cv at p = 0, that is X = Y. Conjecture 1 predicts that the maximising test channels
are a Z-channel and an S-channel; Conjecture 2 predicts that the pair maximising I(X;U,V) are
both Z-channels. Both are proved here for binary U and V, in optimality form: the Challenge
statements exhibit the conjectured channels themselves as `Chan` values and say that no
admissible pair beats them. No admissible pair exceeds the I(U;V) of the Z/S pair
(`conjecture1_p0_holds`), and none undercuts that of the Z/Z pair (`conjecture2_p0_holds`), at
every nondegenerate rate pair. A Z-channel and an S-channel are the same transition matrix up
to relabelling the input alphabet, so what the two conjectures distinguish is the relative
orientation of the two sides: anti-aligned for the maximum, aligned for the minimum.

The development is sorry-free and contains no hand-written axiom declaration.
`averaged_bsc_maximise_mutual_information` and `conjecture2_p0_holds` depend only on `propext`,
`Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`. `conjecture1_p0_holds` additionally depends on exactly one
further axiom: the 24129-monomial Polya certificate of its kernel lemma is checked by
`native_decide`, which on Lean v4.32.0 mints a per-declaration auxiliary axiom
(BSCAveraging.Reflect.kerQPE_allNonneg._native.native_decide.ax_1_1) rather than citing
`Lean.ofReduceBool`; that auxiliary axiom is a custom axiom in Comparator's sense. The other
computed step of that proof, a 650-cell interval sweep, is checked by the Lean kernel and adds
no axiom.

Scope, stated once for all three results. The channels are binary on both sides. For (1) this
is the setting of the source question. For (2) and (3) the reduction of the double-sided
bottleneck over arbitrary alphabets to binary test channels is Proposition 3 of the
Dikshtein-Ordentlich-Shamai paper and Proposition 4.3 of the Pichler-Piantanida-Matz paper; it
is cited here, not formalized, so read as statements about R(Cu, Cv, 0) with unrestricted
alphabets, (2) and (3) are conditional on that published cardinality bound. Conjecture 2 is
stated in its minimisation form, min I(U;V) at fixed rates; the identity
I(U;V) = I(U;X) + I(V;X) - I(X;U,V) that turns the paper's maximisation of I(X;U,V) into
that minimisation is the authors' own, given as Remark 5 of the same paper, and is likewise
not formalized here. Both
conjecture statements are value statements: they say the conjectured optimal value is not
beaten, not that the conjectured pair is the unique optimiser. p = 0 is the only case the
paper's Conjectures 1 and 2 state; Conjecture 3 of that paper, which concerns p above a
threshold, is not addressed.

Two endpoints of (1) were already settled in the literature and are reproved here rather than
established: p = 0, which Pichler-Piantanida-Matz note follows from their Corollary 4.1 and
Proposition 4.3, and the degenerate p = 1/2, where the two regions coincide without
convexification. The new content of (1) is p in (0,1/2) union (1/2,1). The binary restriction
costs nothing in (1): Conjecture 5.2 is stated for S_i, which is defined with the cardinality
bounds |U| <= |X| and |V| <= |Y|, and Proposition 4.3 of the same paper gives
conv(S_i) = conv(R_i).

Novelty has not been independently established. MathOverflow 285151 has no answer and no
comments (StackExchange API, asked 2017-11-03). The Dikshtein-Ordentlich-Shamai paper has one
recorded citing work, a 2024 Entropy editorial that mentions the setting but not the
conjectures, and no resolution of either conjecture was found. Mathlib at the pinned revision
contains no mutual information at all, and no prior Lean formalization of any of the three
problems was found. That search is the authors' own and is not offered as evidence of
priority.

records.title: BrandonMYates/tempered-xi-comparator
records.abstract: This project formalizes in Lean 4 the zero geometry of the odd channel of Riemann's kernel, refuting conjectures of X.-J. Yang (Fractals 32 (2024) 2340116). Let Phi be the kernel of Riemann's integral representation, Phi(u) = sum_{n>=1} (4 pi^2 n^4 e^{9u/2} - 6 pi n^2 e^{5u/2}) e^{-pi n^2 e^{2u}}, the positive even function whose cosh transform is the completed zeta function, and let F(w) = 2 int_0^infty Phi(u) sinh(wu) du be the odd channel of the same kernel; this is Yang's "tempered xi function", in shifted coordinates. Six statements are compared: F is entire; F has infinitely many zeros; every nonzero zero of F has both real and imaginary parts nonzero; the zeros occur in quartets w, -w, conj w, -conj w; consequently the source paper's Conjecture 1, which asserts that every zero of the tempered xi function lies on the line Re s = 1/2, is false, and indeed apart from the origin no zero lies on that line; and the zeros of the sine channel t -> F(it) are not all real, which is the exactly formalizable content of the source paper's Conjecture 2. The audience is the study of real zeros of Fourier transforms of Riemann's kernel, the line of work of Lagarias and Montague (2011), Ki, Kim and Lee (2009), and the de Bruijn-Newman literature: the weight family interpolating the Lagarias-Montague integrated function and the odd xi derivatives places F at weight zero. Yang's conjectures are the occasion for the formalization, not its research context; Conjecture 1 was also the subject of a prize challenge publicly announced by its author, recorded here solely as evidence that the question was regarded as open and difficult, with no claim made concerning the prize itself. This entry makes no claim concerning the Riemann hypothesis. Scope limitation, stated plainly: the compared theorems quantify over the integral F as defined in the Challenge file. The classical identification of F with the odd part of the completed zeta function is NOT proved in Lean; it was checked numerically only (agreement to about forty digits at several complex points), and nothing in the formal development depends on it. On novelty: the refutation of the source conjectures is believed new. In the literature search completed 26 August 2026, every recorded citation of the source paper is a self-citation, the conjectures are restated as open in a 2026 invited review, and no refutation and no proof-assistant formalization of any compared statement was identified; that search is recorded but not exhaustive, and absence from search is not proof of open status. The component statements are not claimed as new: that F is entire of order one with infinitely many zeros was asserted, without proof, by Yang, Abdel-Aty and Geng (Thermal Science 27 (2023) 505-512) for this same function; the exclusion of zeros from the imaginary axis is, in sine-transform coordinates, a 1971 theorem of Spira, independently reproved here, with classical ancestry in Polya (1918, 1926) and Wintner (1935); and the quartet symmetry is recorded as a printed remark by Lagarias and Montague for the sibling weight family. The contribution recorded here is the proof-assistant formalization and its auditable dependency chain. As an aside: the supporting library pinned by this entry also contains a machine-checked counterexample, on the same axiom set, to a log-concavity conjecture of Coffey and Csordas for the derivatives of this same kernel; that theorem is not compared by this configuration and is mentioned only as context for the library.

records.title: BrandonMYates/csordas-comparator
records.abstract: This project formalizes in Lean 4 a counterexample to a log-concavity conjecture of Coffey and Csordas (Math. Comp. 82 (2013) 2265-2272, Conjecture 2.5, where the quantity below is written S_n), later restated as Open Problem 4.13 of Csordas (Comput. Methods Funct. Theory 15 (2015) 373-391). Let Phi be the kernel of Riemann's integral representation, Phi(u) = sum_{n>=1} (4 pi^2 n^4 e^{9u/2} - 6 pi n^2 e^{5u/2}) e^{-pi n^2 e^{2u}}, and set J_n(t) = (Phi^(n)(t))^2 - Phi^(n-1)(t) Phi^(n+1)(t), the n-th Laguerre expression of Phi. The conjecture asserts J_n(t) > 0 for every real t and every n >= 1. The compared theorem proves J_9(0) < 0, refuting it. The mechanism is a single sign anomaly: Phi is even, so Phi^(9)(0) = 0 and J_9(0) = -Phi^(8)(0) Phi^(10)(0); the expected sign alternation of the even-order derivatives at the origin breaks at order ten, with Phi^(8)(0) and Phi^(10)(0) both positive. The formalization defines Phi through its convergent theta series, uses iterated derivatives, and derives evenness from Mathlib's Gaussian Poisson summation. The audience is the study of Laguerre expressions and Turan-type inequalities for the Riemann kernel: the Csordas school and its successors, who posed the conjecture and restated it as an open problem. The result is a counterexample, checkable directly by anyone with the definition of Phi in hand. This entry makes no claim concerning the Riemann hypothesis and no priority claim for the counterexample. Contemporaneous LLM-assisted exact-certificate proofs of the same sign failure are cited in the source metadata; neither is a proof-assistant formalization. The contribution recorded here is the Lean 4 formalization and its auditable dependency chain. As an aside: the supporting library pinned by this entry also contains machine-checked refutations, on the same axiom set, of conjectures of X.-J. Yang (Fractals 32 (2024) 2340116) asserting that the zeros of the tempered xi function -- the odd channel of this same kernel -- are confined to a single line; those theorems are not compared by this configuration and are mentioned only as context for the library.

records.title: GrgAakash/factorial-hypergraph-auxiliary-erdos
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of a quantitative solution to the auxiliary problem suggested by Erdos alongside Problem 1059. Conditional on an explicitly stated standard dimension-one upper-bound sieve theorem, the formalization proves that for every sufficiently large L there are at least ((L+1)!)^eta/(100 log L) integers n in (2L!, (L+1)!] whose prime factors all exceed L and for which n-k! is composite for every 1 <= k <= L. The formalization does not prove that n is prime and therefore does not solve the original Erdos prime problem.

records.title: Arthur742Ramos/finite-graph-fundamental-group
records.abstract: Formalizes the fundamental group of a finite connected graph, represented as a finite weakly connected directed multigraph with its standard interval-cell quotient realization. The main result identifies the topological fundamental group at a chosen vertex with `FreeGroup (Fin (E + 1 - V))`. The proof compares the topological group with the endomorphism group at the root in Mathlib's free groupoid, whose explicit spanning-tree basis supplies the non-tree-edge generators. The development also proves the cycle-rank identities, root-change equivalences, the tree/triviality criterion, and the corresponding abelianization statement. It constructs a path-lifting quiver and verifies its covering property; the realization of that cover is proved contractible by an explicit quotient homotopy, and path lifting plus monodromy completes the comparison isomorphism.

records.title: elliotglazer/nf-not-wpp
records.abstract: A Lean 4 proof that standard first-order New Foundations (NF), axiomatized by extensionality and the full stratified-comprehension schema, syntactically derives the negation of the Weak Partition Principle (WPP). The translated Metamath proof enters through eleven literal Hailperin sentences, which are used internally as a finite-basis bridge and are proved deductively equivalent to standard NF.

records.title: AviKndr/universal-words
records.abstract: Answer to Problem 10.32 of the Kourovka Notebook, posed by Yu. I. Merzlyakov in 1986 and still open in the Notebook's 21st edition (2026), in both directions. Positive direction: there are constants C and N0 such that for all nonzero integers r, s with r or s odd, the word x^r y^s is universal on the symmetric group S_n (every permutation is a value) whenever n >= N0 and n >= C * log m(r,s), where m(r,s) is the product of the distinct primes dividing rs. This is the S_n analogue of the logarithmic Brenner-Evans-Silberger bound for A_n; the best previous S_n bound (Droste, 1986) was linear in m. The constant C is effective (the paper gives 4.65 for its fully effective cases), while the threshold N0 is ineffective solely because the proof uses Vinogradov's three-primes theorem. Negative direction, unconditional: the logarithmic shape is optimal. For r = lcm(1..n) with s its odd part, no element of order 3 in S_n is a value of x^r y^s, while log m(r,s) equals theta(n), the full Chebyshev mass of the primes up to n. The proof is machine-checked in Lean 4 on top of Mathlib, with the complete prose write-up included in this repository. The principal theorem, UniversalWords.kourovka_10_32_conditional, is a fully proved implication from eight explicitly stated published theorems (Herzog-Kaplan-Lev, Boccara, three Rosser-Schoenfeld bounds, Montgomery-Vaughan's Brun-Titchmarsh inequality, Vinogradov's three-primes theorem, and the Halberstam-Richert sieve bound) and depends only on Lean's three standard axioms, as does the optimality theorem UniversalWords.not_universal. A quarantined module assumes the eight statements as axioms to recover the unconditional form.

records.title: hkjtsgmc79-boop/colombo-odd-lean
records.abstract: This project formalizes the odd-exponent branch of Colombo's determinant problem for even matrix size. For every m at least one, every strictly increasing x : Fin (2*m) → ℝ, and every r at least m - 1, it proves that the determinant of the matrix with entries (x_j - x_i)^(2*r+1) is strictly positive. The proof development passes through paired truncated-power determinants, B-spline and Marsden factorization, total nonnegativity, Volterra propagation, and Beta--de Bruijn and Pfaffian identities.

records.title: Vulkin-prog/paper-c-lean
records.abstract: Lean 4 formalization of global and finite-prefix Poisson laws for the starting points of long constant stretches of an extended Rademacher random completely multiplicative function, corresponding to Theorem 16.2 and Corollary 16.4 of the cited source article. The selected declarations give the global interior start-count law on a finite prime-sign cylinder, its recentering at M/2^L, the corresponding theorem on the infinite Rademacher product, and the finite-prefix start-count and longest-stretch law. All asymptotics are uniform in the critical window |L - log_2 M| <= C. Each declaration is conditional on exactly six fully stated ordinary source propositions; those propositions are theorem arguments, not Lean axioms.

records.title: yuma-mizuno/markoff-modp
records.abstract: Lean 4 formalization of strong approximation for the Markoff surface modulo sufficiently large primes. The primary source is Bourgain-Gamburd-Sarnak.

records.title: BrandonMYates/yz-cubic-comparator
records.abstract: This project formalizes in Lean 4 the statement that the Diophantine equation y*z*(y+z) = x^3 + x^2 + 3x - 1 admits no polynomial parametrization over the rationals whose x-coordinate has degree between 1 and 4. Writing f = X^3 + X^2 + 3X - 1, the compared theorem is that there is no triple of rational polynomials (g, u, v) with g nonconstant of degree at most 4 satisfying the identity u*v*(u+v) = f composed with g. Exhibiting such a family is one of the two standard ways an equation of this shape is settled affirmatively -- the other being a sporadic solution -- and the theorem closes that route at low degree. The statement is over the rationals, which is the stronger reading: an integer family is in particular a rational one, so the theorem also excludes integer families in the same degree range. The statement is unconditional and uses no hypothesis from the literature. Context, stated plainly and without overstatement: this equation is recorded on MathOverflow (question 509449, posed by Bogdan Grechuk) as the smallest cubic equation with open solvability problem under the size ordering H(P) = sum |a_i| 2^{d_i} used in that programme, at H = 35. The compared theorem does NOT decide whether the equation has integer solutions, and makes no claim to. A solution could still exist sporadically, or in a polynomial family whose x-coordinate has degree 5 or more, or the equation could be unsolvable for reasons this theorem does not touch. Degree 5 is not covered and is not claimed: it admits slot-degree shapes the argument for degree at most 4 does not reach, and the bound in the statement is exactly the bound that is proved. The audience is the programme that maintains and closes the frontier list this equation sits on -- Bogdan Grechuk and Ashleigh Ratcliffe, On the shortest open cubic equations (arXiv:2603.29831), and the MathOverflow thread 466803 that tracks the current smallest open equations -- together with the adjacent literature on cubic Diophantine equations of this shape: Janos Kollar and Jennifer Li on the Mordell-Schinzel conjecture for cubic Diophantine equations XYZ = G(X,Y) (arXiv:2412.12080), and Martin Bright and Julian Lyczak on log K3 surfaces (arXiv:1705.04529), whose setting -- a del Pezzo surface minus a smooth anticanonical divisor -- is the geometry of the affine surface defined by this equation. Ruling out low-degree parametric families is directly responsive to how equations on that frontier list are resolved. On novelty: a literature search recorded 2026-07-21 and repeated 2026-08-26 identified no indexed resolution of the equation and no proof-assistant formalization touching it or the frontier list; the search is recorded but not exhaustive, and absence from search is not proof of open status. That search establishes that the equation is open; it does NOT establish that the non-existence of low-degree polynomial families is a new observation, and no such claim is made here. The contribution recorded by this entry is the proof-assistant formalization and its auditable dependency chain.

records.title: nielstron/langlib
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of grammar and automaton presentations of the extended Chomsky hierarchy. Starting from unrestricted-grammar rewriting, it defines regular, linear, context-free, context-sensitive, indexed, deterministic context-free, recursive, and recursively enumerable language classes; relates finite, pushdown, linearly bounded, and Mathlib TM0 automata to the corresponding grammar classes; proves strict hierarchy inclusions; and establishes closure or non-closure under thirteen operations for seven major classes.

records.title: sneed-and-feed/lean-theorems-1
records.abstract:
A complete, machine-checked Lean 4 formalization of Hall's Marriage Theorem (Philip Hall 1935, Halmos–Vaughan 1950; Freek Wiedijk #87). Proves that an indexed family of finite sets admits a system of distinct representatives (SDR) if and only if Hall's marriage condition holds.
To the maintainers' knowledge, the theorem was not found in an exact declaration name,
    docstring, and type signature search of the pinned Mathlib revision (Mathlib v4.34.0-rc1).

records.title: Arthur742Ramos/jacobian-conjecture-lean
records.abstract: An independent Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of the explicit three-dimensional polynomial map announced by Levent Alpöge in 2026. The project proves that its formal Jacobian determinant is the nonzero constant -2, verifies an explicit three-point fibre over the complex numbers, and derives the failure of injectivity required to refute the dimension-three Jacobian conjecture. The source formulas and proof scope are recorded explicitly; no claim is made about the still-open two-dimensional case.
authors: Ruy J. G. B. de Queiroz

records.title: sneed-and-feed/lean-theorems-1
records.abstract: A machine-checked Lean 4 formalization of the general n-dimensional combinatorial Sperner parity theorem on abstract n-dimensional pseudomanifolds with boundary for arbitrary dimension n : ℕ. Proves the local door-counting parity invariant on (n+1)-simplices, the global double-counting identity on door-facet incidences, and the master parity congruence modulo 2 relating panchromatic (n+1)-simplices to boundary doors. The theorem is conditional on an odd number of boundary (n-1)-doors; obtaining the classical geometric Sperner lemma for simplicial subdivisions of geometric simplices with boundary-preserving colorings is a specialization requiring an additional geometric boundary induction argument not contained in these abstract combinatorial declarations. This n-dimensional development (SpernerND.lean) generalizes and supersedes the fixed-dimensional combinatorial parity identities in the repository's lower-dimensional modules (SpernersLemma.lean and Sperner3D.lean) into a single unified parameterized architecture. To the maintainers' knowledge, the theorem was not found in an exact declaration name, docstring, and type signature search of the pinned Mathlib revision (Mathlib v4.34.0-rc1).

records.title: Arthur742Ramos/HigherLambdaModel
records.abstract: A Lean formalization of higher-dimensional structure in the untyped lambda calculus.  Arthur Ramos is the first author and responsible maintainer of the Lean formalization; Daniel O. Martinez-Rivillas and Ruy J.G.B. de Queiroz are credited as the mathematical/source authors whose results are formalized.  The Palomar surface uses a restricted Kan-complex exponential and a separate certificate for term-generated semantic bodies, while the substantive repository also formalizes the higher conversion tower and the concrete K-infinity homotopy lambda model.

records.title: sneed-and-feed/lean-theorems-1
records.abstract: A complete machine-checked Lean 4 formalization of Descartes's Rule of Signs (1637, Wiedijk #73). Proves that for any non-zero real polynomial p(X) over ℝ, the number of positive real roots counted with algebraic multiplicity is bounded above by the number of sign variations in its coefficient sequence (ignoring zero coefficients), and their difference is an even non-negative integer. While the pinned Mathlib revision (Mathlib v4.34.0-rc1) contains the upper-bound inequality in `Mathlib.Algebra.Polynomial.RuleOfSigns` (`Polynomial.roots_countP_pos_le_signVariations`), this development formalizes the complete two-part theorem by proving the even-parity conclusion (Gauss 1828), establishing the sign-variation parity correspondence with leading and trailing coefficients, and providing a direct list-based coefficient sequence interface.

records.title: Arthur742Ramos/SpinorLean
records.abstract: Formalizes an exterior-model spinor construction for a field K in which 2 is invertible, using an explicit hyperbolic presentation and the Clifford conjugation action on the ambient quadratic space.  The development proves field-sensitive covering and image results: the positive split-rank spin-to-isometry kernel is {1,-1}, the spin action therefore descends only projectively, the split-line image is exactly the square-scaling subgroup, and a finite-dimensional split Levi element associated to g lies in the ambient spin image exactly when det(g) is a square unit.  The repository also packages the chosen exterior model, half-spin pieces, explicit transvection and square-scaling Clifford lifts, square-class quotient characters, vector-product norm identities, and selected complex and real low-dimensional Clifford classifications.
authors: Ruy J. G. B. de Queiroz

records.title: shaikidris/CollatzEndpointTransport-Palomar
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of a quantitative stability theorem for the one-block endpoint-pullback operator of the shortcut Collatz map. If an arbitrary target set has at most C N^(1-D) exceptions among the positive integers up to N, then, for every central Renyi order 1/2 < theta < 1, every admissible fixed central window, and every positive transport coefficient below the explicit asymptotic slope, its pullback through one floor(log_2 n)-step endpoint is (K(C+1)D^(-(1+theta)), transport*D)-dense whenever D is sufficiently small. The cutoff and K depend only on the fixed moment and transport parameters, not on the target set or C,D. This is an operator-level arbitrary-target theorem, not a pointwise convergence or eventual-descent claim.

records.title: yuhangshi888/sun-cotangent-permanent-counterexample-lean
records.abstract: A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of the exact evaluation of the normalized 14 by 14 cotangent permanent at p = 29. The formalization proves that its value is 84643985981440 and hence gives a counterexample to the cotangent sign inequality in Zhi-Wei Sun's Conjecture 4.7(ii). It includes the analytic-to-cyclotomic bridge, two separately kernel-checked finite permanent certificates, Chinese-remainder and coefficientwise integer lifting, the Section 3 Archimedean uniqueness argument, and equation (4.1) in the integral cyclotomic quotient.

records.title: BrandonMYates/schwarzschild-comparator
records.abstract: Twenty-one theorems and thirty-three definitions, machine-checked in Lean 4 against Mathlib v4.32.0: the Schwarzschild, Schwarzschild-de Sitter (Kottler), Reissner-Nordstrom (with the Maxwell stress tensor defined and G = 8 pi T proved in all sixteen components), ingoing Vaidya (null dust of rank at most one, rank one wherever dm/dv ≠ 0, for a merely once-differentiable mass function), spatially flat FLRW (both Friedmann equations in Einstein-tensor form), static de Sitter, Minkowski-in-spherical and Kiselev metrics, together with Birkhoff uniqueness in the areal static gauge and the n != 2 equivalence of the two forms of the vacuum equations. The results are classical and NO NEW MATHEMATICS IS CLAIMED: this is a proof of concept for the definitions. Lean checks that a proof establishes a statement, not that a definition means what its name says, so the entry certifies its sign, index and contraction conventions by computing textbook solutions with them -- including four NONZERO answers (de Sitter R = 12/L^2, Reissner-Nordstrom R_thetatheta = Q^2/r^2, Vaidya R_vv = 2 (dm/dv)/r^2, Kiselev R_thetatheta = -3wc r^-(3w+1)), because a curvature definition that was accidentally identically zero would still prove every vacuum theorem here. Scope: everything is a computation in ONE FIXED CHART, an open subset of R^4 -- no atlas, no manifold, no coordinate-independence theorem, no maximal extension, and horizons and coordinate poles lie outside every statement. NOT compared: Ricci symmetry R_bd = R_db in general (it needs Clairaut for the coordinate partial derivative, which Mathlib supplies only for fderiv) or the Bianchi identities; Maxwell's own equations; any matter model, fluid or energy condition beyond the single defined Maxwell stress tensor; non-flat FLRW; the outgoing Vaidya chart. Audience: general relativists, for whom this is the definitional layer a junction-condition or thin-shell statement would be written against, and the formalization community, for whom it is coverage-creating rather than coverage-duplicating. Mathlib v4.32.0 contains no curvature of any kind -- christoffel, ricci, scalarCurvature, Lorentzian, PseudoRiemannian and five further names return zero hits across all 8,264 .lean files at the pinned revision, and its one metric structure hard-codes positive definiteness -- so the entire chain is defined inline in the Challenge.

records.title: yuningyang19/parameter_free_gradient_p
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of three results about exact value-gradient oracle complexity in finite-dimensional l_p geometry: strict-local scale-identification impossibility at fixed LR/epsilon = 4, the known-parameter p > 2 upper/lower exponent p/(p+2) with its stated horizon and dimension qualifications, and a post-secant-initialization parameter-free runtime family with the three p regimes. The Comparator surface contains exactly these three declarations; the other certified results remain supporting proof infrastructure.

records.title: Arthur742Ramos/NagataFactoriality
records.abstract: A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of Nagata's factoriality theorem for noetherian integral domains.  It proves that unique factorization descends from a localization when every denominator is a finite product of prime elements, packages the specialization to submonoids generated by sets of primes, and demonstrates the method with a Nagata-based polynomial UFD theorem.
authors: Ruy J. G. B. de Queiroz

records.title: ehrlich-b/euclidean-jordan
records.abstract: The Jordan trace form tau(x,y) = tr(L_{x*y}), constructed from the multiplication rather than assumed: symmetric, associative, and positive definite. Symmetry and associativity need neither finite dimensionality nor formal reality; positive definiteness needs both, and runs through the spectral theorem. The carrier is not assumed unital, so this supplies the Euclidean form itself and does not by itself establish a unital Euclidean Jordan algebra. Sits directly on Mathlib's IsCommJordan. Coordinatization is absent. Machine checked, not peer reviewed, no priority claim.

records.title: dcposch/jc2-lean
records.abstract: Lean 4 / Mathlib proof of the source-facing polynomial-cube exclusion at actual partial degrees (6,9).  From literal bivariate polynomials of outer degrees six and nine, leading coefficients s^6 and s^9 for a common polynomial s, and nonzero constant Keller bracket, the formalization proves that no such source exists, including when s is constant.  It constructs the finite-pole or infinity expansion, exhausts every timing of the eight Faber loads through rho2, and excludes the remaining elliptic, cusp, zero-invariant, and constant-core terminal fibres.  It does not claim the reduction from an arbitrary Keller pair, all (6,9), maximum eleven, or the plane Jacobian conjecture.

records.title: Arthur742Ramos/dinitz-garg-goemans-counterexample-lean
records.abstract: A standalone Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of the finite counterexample to the cost-preserving single-source unsplittable-flow conjecture. The development realizes a directed graph with seven vertices, nine arcs, and three terminal demands; checks a feasible rational fractional flow of cost 58 with maximum demand 15; and proves that every unsplittable routing under the weak additive congestion bound has cost at least 60. It also derives the failure of the strict congestion variant. No general algorithmic or complexity-theoretic claim is made.
authors: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

records.title: yuhangshi888/zeta-simple-zeros-673316977
records.abstract: A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of the supporting-plane and exact-arithmetic portion of the finite-dimensional argument in Yuhang Shi's research draft on simple zeros of the Riemann zeta function. It proves a conditional scalar two-certificate supporting-plane implication, its explicit piecewise-square-root specialization at block length 219, and the exact strict comparison above 673316977/10^9 for the resulting local assembly expression. The spectral derivation of the trace-envelope alternative, the upstream seven- and nine-point interval certificates, and the analytic passage from finite blocks to a global zeta-zero proportion are not formalized here and are not claimed as Palomar-verified conclusions.

records.title: Arthur742Ramos/TopologicalComputationalPaths
records.abstract: A Lean formalization of topological semantics for endpoint-varying computational paths.  It constructs both the canonical final composable quotient and the ordinary pullback of quotient arrows.  The selected result proves that the canonical comparison is a continuous bijection and characterizes exactly when it is quotient, a homeomorphism, and an induced topology agreement; under these equivalent conditions ordinary composition is continuous.  It also records discontinuity as an obstruction and proves compact--Hausdorff and discrete sufficient cases.  The selected certificate additionally requires full additive classifications of the genuine based-loop spaces `AddCircle (1 : ℝ)` by `ℤ` and its product torus by `ℤ × ℤ`: the invariant, identity value, composition additivity, explicit standard representatives, and both inverse laws are checked using covering-map lifts and coordinatewise arguments.  It also formalizes the observable based fiber of the universal continuous-path presentation, its homeomorphism to the standard based loop quotient, the final/ordinary pair comparison, and the source-backed Hawaiian-earring transfer: the non-quotient square and discontinuous multiplication force failure of the scoped ordinary-pair quotient, topology agreement, and ordinary multiplication continuity under the comparison.
authors: Ruy J. G. B. de Queiroz

records.title: nimaanari/formalization-beyond-bethe
records.abstract: Computing or approximating the permanent is a canonical problem in theoretical computer science and in counting and sampling.  Before this work, the canonical Bethe approximation gave the best known deterministic guarantee, with approximation factor (sqrt 2)^n.  This formalization proves that there is an absolute constant c < sqrt 2 and a deterministic polynomial-time c^n-approximation for every nonnegative rational matrix. It checks the mathematical and algorithmic proof down to Lean's standard logical axioms, including the finite-precision convex-optimization implementation.

records.title: sneed-and-feed/lean-theorems-1
records.abstract: A complete, machine-checked Lean 4 formalization of Radon's Lemma (Johann Radon, 1921) and Helly's Theorem on intersecting families of convex sets (Eduard Helly, 1923; Freek Wiedijk #99) from first principles. Proves that any d + 2 points in ℝ^d admit a Radon partition into two disjoint subsets whose convex hulls intersect, and uses Radon's lemma by induction on the family size to prove Helly's theorem for finite families of convex sets under the general <= d + 1 subfamily intersection hypothesis (covering small families |ι| <= d + 1 as well as large families). To the maintainers' knowledge, the theorem was not found in an exact declaration name, docstring, and type signature search of the pinned Mathlib revision (Mathlib v4.34.0-rc1).

records.title: ehrlich-b/euclidean-jordan
records.abstract: The frame Peirce decomposition: relative to a Jordan frame, a Euclidean Jordan algebra is the internal direct sum of the blocks V_ij over unordered pairs of frame indices, and in finite dimension the diagonal blocks are lines, dim V_ii = 1 - the Faraut-Koranyi table entry. The frame is carried as data, so frame conjugacy is sidestepped and nothing here claims anything about the rank of J. Machine checked, not peer reviewed, no priority claim.

records.title: Arthur742Ramos/hadamard-668-lean
records.abstract: An independent Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of a supplied bordered block-circulant sign matrix of order 668.  The main theorem proves that there exists a 668 by 668 integer matrix with entries in {-1, 1}, diagonal row norm 668, and zero inner product between every pair of distinct rows. The formalization is a certificate-specific existence result, not a classification of Hadamard matrices and not a proof of the general Hadamard conjecture.
authors: Ruy J. G. B. de Queiroz

records.title: BochaoKong/classical-complex-wpt
records.abstract: A Mathlib-only Lean 4 formalization of the classical complex-analytic Weierstrass preparation theorem at the origin. For every number of base variables and every preparation degree, including the zero-dimensional and degree-zero cases, it constructs the distinguished monic polynomial and nonvanishing analytic unit and proves uniqueness of all factors as germs.

records.title: mccorvie/classification-of-surfaces
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the classification theorem for compact connected topological 2-manifolds, including surfaces with boundary. The main theorem proves that every compact connected Hausdorff 2-manifold modeled on the Euclidean half-plane is homeomorphic to the sphere, an orientable canonical quotient surface, or a non-orientable canonical quotient surface. The submitted theorem is the exact statement of the Lean Eval `topological_classification_of_surfaces` challenge.

records.title: sneed-and-feed/lean-theorems-1
records.abstract: A complete, machine-checked Lean 4 formalization of Bárány's Colorful Carathéodory Theorem (1982), Bárány's First Selection Lemma (1982), the 1D Centerpoint Theorem, and geometric deductions from first principles. Proves that for any d + 1 sets of points S_0, ..., S_d in R^d whose convex hulls all contain a common target point p, there exists a colorful transversal f (selecting f(i) in S_i for each color class i) whose convex hull conv({f(0), ..., f(d)}) contains p. Formulated over arbitrary dimension d, with specializations to the origin and low dimensions (d = 0, 1, 2), a formal deduction of the classical Carathéodory theorem bound, the 1D Centerpoint Theorem (median contains >= floor((n+1)/2) = ceil(n/2) points in each half-line), Bárány's 1982 First Selection Lemma (>= (|P|/2)(|P|-|P|/2) pairs containing the centerpoint), and the 1D Colorful Selection Lemma (at least one colorful pair covering p). To the maintainers' knowledge, the theorem was not found in an exact declaration name, docstring, and type signature search of the pinned Mathlib revision (Mathlib v4.34.0-rc1).

records.title: sneed-and-feed/lean-theorems-1
records.abstract: A comprehensive, machine-checked Lean 4 formalization of the Erdős–Szekeres Convex Polygon Theorem (1935). Formalizes orientation determinants, general position, 2D rotation transformations with finite slope avoidance (rotating any finite set to have mutually distinct x-coordinates), x-coordinate sorting, cup-cap sequences with Pascal-type binomial split recurrences, halfspace separation for convex hulls, and rotation invariance of convex polygons. Proves that any finite set of at least choose(2k - 4, k - 2) + 1 points in general position in ℝ² contains the vertices of a strictly convex k-gon, verifying the Happy Ending Theorem under pure general position with no distinct-x-coordinate restriction. To the maintainers' knowledge, the theorem was not found in an exact declaration name, docstring, and type signature search of the pinned Mathlib revision (Mathlib v4.34.0-rc1).

records.title: ukiyois/hs-virial-nbc-identity
records.abstract: A kernel-checked Lean formalization of the exact no-broken-circuit volume identity for hard-sphere Mayer cluster integrals and the stronger dimension-three fork-packing upper bound for each tree-owned NBC region. The development proves finite broken-circuit cancellation, the measurable finite-region decomposition, the anchored Euclidean product-measure theorem, and its explicit flat-coordinate transport.  Its geometric result is the attachment-aware estimate Vol(NBC_T) <= (17/32)^hardSphereNu T * hardSphereKappa^(k-1), where hardSphereNu T is the maximum cardinality of a packing of pairwise vertex-disjoint, order-compatible forks in T.  A formal fork is an ordered triple (a,b,c) with a < b < c, center a, leaves b,c, and tree edges {a,b} and {a,c}.  The central contribution is the complete pointwise-to-integral bridge together with the orientation-aware measure-preserving factorization that realizes the per-fork volume suppression.

records.title: ehrlich-b/composition-algebras
