records.title: shaikidris/prime-star-spectra-formalization
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the ordered adjacency spectrum of finite prime-cover graphs. Its root-centred specialization proves that the square of the largest ordered eigenvalue equals pi(X) plus four times the finite prime sum of 1/(p-1), up to o(1). More generally, for every fixed finite set S of deleted primes and epsilon > 0, the same law with the explicit centre correction c(a) holds uniformly over allowed centres a <= (log X)^(1/2-epsilon). The same window admits a uniform centre--shell evolution theorem at the explicit first-exit frequency, with a finite localization-plus-phase error bound.

records.title: pengzhang91/Feige
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the sharp unit-slack (delta = 1) small-deviation inequality for sums of independent nonnegative random variables. For every positive integer n and every independent family X_1, ..., X_n of measurable, integrable, nonnegative random variables satisfying E[X_i] <= 1, writing S = sum_i X_i, it proves the sharp bound P(S < E[S] + 1) >= (n / (n + 1))^n and proves that this constant is optimal for each fixed n. This optimal dimension-dependent bound strengthens and implies Feige's 1/e conjecture. The repository also formalizes the Vlassis-Thomas exact calibration theorem and Grünbaum's centroid-halfspace inequality used in the proof.

records.title: JD-Jones-ASES/Hadamard-formal
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the periodic Cooper-Wallis construction and of Hadamard existence at eight orders: from kernel-checked periodic T-matrix quadruples of orders 103 and 163 and seven symmetric-circulant Williamson quadruples, the development proves that Hadamard matrices of orders 2884, 4532, 7004, 7172, 7828, 8476, 9476, and 11948 exist. Each of the eight orders lands on an entry of Table 4 of Cati and Pasechnik's maintained construction database (arXiv:2411.18897v2, 2025-08-30) recording no Hadamard matrix of that order as known, and the source repositories' firsthand audit of the construction literature (closed 2026-08-29) located no published route to the order-103 or order-163 T-objects the eight are built from. The development also proves the erratum core of the companion Hadamard-M note on Miyamoto's 1991 construction paper: the handshake parity obstruction, its empty-class corollary, and the nonexistence of the displayed C2-matrix ingredient of that paper's Corollary 4 at every positive block order not congruent to 1 mod 4 - covering the paper's printed list entries at orders 103, 127, and 151 under both printed readings of the corollary's output order, and leaving the order-515 list entry, the paper's claim of a Hadamard matrix of order 2060, unsupported by the paper's own machinery. Cati and Pasechnik, for want of details, record being unable to verify the constructions claimed in that paper's section 7, naming order 4*515 as their example; the obstruction supplies an independent mathematical reason the printed route cannot deliver that entry. Order 2060 itself is not open: a Hadamard matrix of that order was posted publicly on 2026-08-23, credited to Schneider, by other means.

records.title: Arthur742Ramos/GraphCoveringTheory
records.abstract: Formalizes the sharp Schreier index formula for a finite-index subgroup of a free group on a finite nonempty generating type. For a finite nonempty type alpha, a subgroup H of FreeGroup alpha with finite index d is proved equivalent, as a group, to FreeGroup (Fin (1 + d * (card alpha - 1))). More strongly, the repository exposes a FreeGroupBasis for H with this indexing type. The proof realizes H as the vertex group of the finite action-groupoid covering on the coset space, verifies the covering locally by explicit star and costar bijections, and counts the complement of a geodesic spanning tree. It also exposes the truncation-safe natural-number statement and the generic finite free-groupoid rank calculation used by the submission theorem. For finite-index normal subgroups, a companion module proves that every deck transformation of the finite Schreier action is a unique right translation by the quotient group.

Uses the polynomial linear algebra method over ZMod p to prove both the general non-uniform bound |F| <= sum_{i=0}^s choose(n, i) and the uniform cardinality bound |F| <= choose(n, s). records.title: stalex444/mahler-measure-minima
records.abstract: For each degree d in {2, 3, 4}, the polynomial x^d - x - 1 attains the minimal Mahler measure among monic irreducible integer polynomials of degree d with Mahler measure above one, and the three minimal values are exactly the golden ratio (M^2 = M + 1), the plastic ratio (M^3 = M + 1), and the root of x^4 - x^3 - 1 above one (M^4 = M^3 + 1); by Siegel's classical theorem (1944, cited as background, not formalized here) the latter two are the smallest and second-smallest Pisot numbers. Classically the degree-4 minimizer is not itself a Pisot polynomial, yet its measure lands back on the Pisot list via the reciprocal transform. The minimizers' irreducibility is part of the compared surface. Proofs are by a Graeffe-certificate architecture: an effective coefficient-bound box from Mathlib's norm_coeff_le_choose_mul_mahlerMeasure, then one integer certificate per box element (tie orbit, cyclotomic cofactor, explicit factorization, or an iterated Graeffe coefficient bound), 6,171 + 147 + 21 certificates kernel-decided with plain decide — no native_decide anywhere. The exact values follow from a root-inversion identity and a (sigma, s)-reduction localizing the conjugate pairs, with multiplicity excluded by kernel-certified measure brackets.

records.title: MaxWellApexLab/BicausalOT-palomar
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the Bellman value representation for bicausal optimal transport, together with the descriptive-set-theoretic library it requires.  The result registered by this Comparator configuration is the Kuratowski–Ryll-Nardzewski measurable selection theorem: for an arbitrary measurable space (alpha, A) and a Polish space Y, a multifunction Phi : alpha -> Set Y with nonempty closed values that is weakly measurable (the hit set {a | Phi a meets U} lies in A for every open U) admits an A-to-Borel measurable selection f with f a in Phi a for every a.  The statement is measure-free and pointwise: no measure appears, and the selection property holds everywhere, not almost everywhere.  It is proved from Mathlib alone, by the classical argument — a dense sequence in Y, a recursion producing measurable countably-valued approximate selectors whose successive stages stay within (1/2)^n, and a uniform Cauchy limit that is measurable as a pointwise limit of measurable functions and lands in Phi a because Phi a is closed.  The measurability of each refinement step is obtained by splitting over the countably many measurable fibres of the previous stage's index function, on each of which the test set is cut out by a fixed open set, so the weak measurability hypothesis applies directly.  No measurable selection theorem exists in Mathlib at the pinned revision.  The wider repository contains the Bellman value representation for bicausal optimal transport in one period and over a general finite horizon, an epsilon-optimal strategy that is sigma(Sigma-1-1)-measurable at every stage and an exactly optimal Borel-measurable strategy under Feller kernels and lower semicontinuous costs (Bertsekas–Shreve 7.50 and 8.3), and the supporting descriptive set theory: Jankov–von Neumann uniformization, Choquet capacitability for analytic sets, Polishness of the space of probability measures on a Polish space, and lower semianalyticity of kernel integrals.  The measurable selection theorem is used in that development to produce plain-Borel-measurable feasible bicausal strategies.
